nodes.name: Sandbox User
nodes.description: Human or orchestrating agent who logs in at the IdP and asks mediatore for a sandbox. Never talks to Kubernetes, SPIRE or the hypervisor directly; the broker is the only front door for delegated sandboxes.

nodes.name: Identity Provider (Dex, Google, Auth0, Entra ID)
nodes.description: Upstream OIDC issuer, any the configuration names (ADR-0017): Dex bridging GitHub or LDAP, Google, Auth0, all on the session path (a public PKCE client, the refresh grant before every issue, ADR-0013); Entra ID also performs the On-Behalf-Of exchange (ADR-0016): the caller's access token for mediatore is exchanged at claim creation for a refresh token issued to mediatore for that user, and every token issue is a refresh_token grant naming the audience's resource. mediatore's own STS stands in for delegation on issuers without one (ADR-0003).

nodes.name: mediatore
nodes.description: The identity broker: one binary, two listeners (user-facing bearer HTTPS behind the ingress, sandbox-facing SPIFFE mTLS terminated in-process on aws-lc-rs), a claim watcher and a token backend per audience (ADR-0002, ADR-0003, ADR-0007). Runs as a restricted, non-root Deployment in mediatore-system, a namespace of its own that the base ships labelled for Pod Security restricted (ADR-0056): it holds the broker, its keys, the store's Secrets, SandboxNode and PolicyFloor resources, the watcher's Lease and the admission parameter that names the broker, and nothing of banlieue's or a tenant's. The home namespace is the pod's own and never configuration; the broker refuses to start when it is default and warns when a claimable namespace is its home. Its ClusterSPIFFEID selects that namespace, the pod label, the ServiceAccount and the container name. Its SVID lives only in process memory.

nodes.name: User API (bearer)
nodes.description: POST/GET/DELETE /v1/claims. Validates the caller's IdP token (issuer, audience, signature via JWKS, group gate: one of required_group, required_groups or an explicit allow_any_authenticated, ADR-0046) and creates an AgentSandbox with spec.subject taken from the validated token (ADR-0008). The namespace is decided here, at TB-1 (ADR-0046): with sandboxes.namespaces set (a namespace-to-groups map in the broker's configuration, not a node), the request must name a namespace and the caller's token groups must intersect that namespace's groups, read only from a token of an issuer the entry lists (ADR-0074: with two or more issuers every entry lists its issuers or the broker does not start; an unlisted issuer gets the unqualified caller's answer), else 403 (one body for an unlisted and an unqualified namespace); an omitted namespace is 400 namespace_required; without the map it is the single sandboxes.namespace as before. GET and DELETE take ?namespace= and apply the same group check plus the owner check (a namespace outside the map or not the caller's is 404). ADR-0053: an audience scoped to namespaces (audiences[].namespaces, each entry that namespace's rules, the audience's own rules the ceiling every entry must sit inside) is refused to a namespace it does not list as 400 unknown_audience, the same answer as an audience that does not exist, and a claim's routes, the gateway's routes and every mint read the claim record's own namespace. Phase 2 (policy.audiences: shadow by default, enforce): the claim must name a policy that resolves to a verified, unexpired bundle (400 policy_required, 400 unknown_policy, 503 policy_not_synced until every watched namespace was listed), the bundle must grant each audience (400 unknown_audience) and its lease cover ttl_seconds (400 ttl_exceeds_policy), and a claim's rules, endpoints and credential lifetime are the bundle's grant bounded by the audience's own rules (the ceiling), read from the claim's current bundle at every ask, so a missing, expired or unverified bundle takes the audiences away. GET answers from the resource's status, DELETE deletes it and the finalizer does the rest. Under dev_mode the in-memory store and dev binder stand in. crates/mediatore-api + mediatore-entra. Since ADR-0045 also GET /v1/claims/{name}/logs (NDJSON, follow, since, tail): the stored output of the caller's own claim, the same subject and namespace checks, 501 unless logs.enabled, one audit line per read and never the content; and POST /v1/claims refuses workload.logs: true with 501 when logs are off.

nodes.name: Sandbox API (SPIFFE mTLS)
nodes.description: POST /v1/nodes, GET /v1/me, POST /v1/me/report, POST /v1/me/exit (ADR-0033: the workload's exit recorded, the claim released as a delete releases it), POST /v1/token over SPIFFE mTLS: client certificate required, chain verified against the trust-domain bundle, peer SPIFFE ID taken from the verified URI SAN and restricted to /banlieue/node/*, /banlieue/claim/* and, since ADR-0053, the gateway authorizer's identity spiffe://<td>/gateway/authorizer (Naming::is_gateway_authorizer), which the gateway routes alone accept; the gateway listeners' identity spiffe://<td>/gateway, admitted from ADR-0028 until then, no longer completes a handshake, other than while the transition switch accept_plain_gateway_identity is on. A connection ends at its peer certificate's notAfter. Node identities may register and fetch their subject, claim identities may request audience-scoped tokens (minted by the STS or Entra, or since ADR-0032 the operator's own credential for an audience via: secret, handed with the header it goes in). The dev header exists only under dev_mode on a loopback listener (ADR-0007). crates/mediatore-api. GET /v1/me also carries the operator's pull credential for the registry the claim's image names, and no other (ADR-0022). ADR-0040: POST /v1/gateway/claims/{uid}/credential, accepted only from the gateway authorizer's identity (ADR-0053), returns an audience's credential for the gateway to place when the audience is inject: gateway; POST /v1/token refuses such an audience with 403 placed_at_gateway; GET /v1/gateway/claims/{uid} carries the gateway-placed routes (endpoint, rules, header names, non-secret extra headers) and GET /v1/me carries credential: gateway and the inject port on those routes. Since ADR-0045 also POST /v1/me/logs: the claim's node ships the redacted workload output, accepted only for a claim that opted in, shape- and size-checked, rate-limited to two batches a second, idempotent on the sequence number, a follower of the claim woken once the batch is stored, 501 unless logs.enabled. ADR-0061: GET /v1/me, POST /v1/token and the gateway's claim answer and credential first check that a running claim is still inside its policy's current bundle (the lease, the policy's name, nothing the guest rendered wider); under policy.follow: enforce with policy.audiences: enforce a claim outside it is 403 policy_changed at the mint and 404 at the gateway, final for the claim; under shadow the verdict is recorded and nothing refused. ADR-0062: POST /v1/gateway/decisions, accepted only from the gateway authorizer's identity, takes one gateway's batch of tunnel and inject decisions (claim, kind, authority, audience, verdict, reason, where the allowlist came from, and the gateway's self-declared name) and writes one info line per decision after a shape check of the whole batch; nothing is stored.

nodes.name: Claim Watcher and AgentSandbox Reconciler
nodes.description: Reconciles AgentSandbox (ADR-0008, built): creates and owns one VirtualMachineClaim per sandbox, named after it, at most once; writes the store record keyed by the claim's UID; mirrors the claim's status plus whether the entry is set (Ready only when Bound and set); refuses, before any claim exists, a sandbox naming an audience or issuer outside mediatore's configuration; holds a finalizer that releases the record, deletes the claim and lets the object go only once the claim is gone. Watches VirtualMachineClaim (managed-by label) and VirtualMachine (pool members): on Bound resolves the node by the EK hash the claim mirrors (never by name, address or UUID), binds through the Reconciler, fails an unresolved bind after a bounded wait by deleting the claim, releases on Releasing / Failed / deletion and at resync; declares a node entry when a member publishes its vTPM endorsement certificate; one replica leads by Lease (ADR-0011, built). Under ADR-0026 (implemented) the same loop reflects notaio's bundle ConfigMaps in the configured namespaces, verifies each against the configured keys, moves the policy's version floor in the store by a compare and set, caches the verified payload, and on each reconcile of a sandbox, and whenever its policy's bundle changes, reports every way the broker would allow more than the bundle (codes P001 to P012) as a log line and the PolicyConformant condition; in shadow it admits, binds and mints exactly as before; under policy.egress: enforce the bundle's servable direct egress is added to the claim's routes at the gateway (ADR-0030), and a gateway-placed audience must be one the claim's policy admits (ADR-0040). Since ADR-0054 a sandbox's policyRef is resolved only in the namespaces its own namespace draws from (policy.sources in the broker's configuration, a mapping from sandbox namespace to policy namespaces; by default the sandbox's own namespace alone, never a fallback across policy.namespaces): a name in no source is P011, a name held by two sources is P012, and both read the same for a policy elsewhere and a policy nowhere; under enforce such a sandbox is Failed with policy_not_resolved before any claim exists and a sandbox whose sources are not yet read is held, while in shadow it is created and reported. Never holds a SPIRE admin identity (ADR-0006). crates/mediatore-claims.

nodes.name: STS
nodes.description: Self-issued ES256 tokens with an RFC 8693 act claim naming the claim SVID as actor; JWKS derived from the signing key and served at /.well-known/jwks.json. Used for audiences whose backend is `sts` (ADR-0003). Since ADR-0071 `sub` is the subject id behind its issuer's subject_prefix when the issuer has one: under an sts with two or more issuers every issuer carries a prefix and no two overlap, or the broker does not start, so the same id at two issuers is two different subs; one issuer with no prefix keeps the bare id. Since ADR-0073 the same prefix qualifies each element of groups, from the same lookup, so a token never carries a qualified sub beside bare groups; the broker's own decisions read the raw groups. crates/mediatore-sts.

nodes.name: AgentSandbox resources
nodes.description: Namespaced CRD mediatore.io/v1beta1 (v1alpha1 until ADR-0048, 2026-11-18; v1alpha1 served beside it as the same object, deprecated, conversion None, ADR-0049), served and reconciled by mediatore (ADR-0008, built: roadmap 08; created through the broker only in a namespace of sandboxes.namespaces that the caller's groups admit, ADR-0046; schema generated from the Rust type into deploy/base/crds). The request for one sandbox: subject, poolRef or poolSelector (exactly one, by CEL; poolSelector: {} is every pool in the namespace, an omitted field never is; the pool bound from is mirrored into status.poolRef, ADR-0044), selection (optional; strategy LongestReady, MostAvailable or Spread, how banlieue ranks the Ready members of the matched pools; absent is LongestReady and mediatore writes no default; copied to the claim verbatim, ADR-0047), ttlSeconds, audiences, workload. Created by the user API on POST /v1/claims or declaratively by anything with RBAC on agentsandboxes; spec.subject is pinned to the caller by the mediatore-agentsandbox-subject admission policy unless the caller is mediatore's ServiceAccount or a listed broker, and the whole spec is immutable afterwards. Since ADR-0072 the policy refuses an issuer its issuerPrefixes does not list once that list is set, and a list that cannot tell its issuers apart admits nothing; the annotation mediatore.io/front-door: api marks a sandbox the broker created through POST /v1/claims, admitted from the broker's username alone and immutable, and the reconciler refuses a sandbox without it whose issuer is outside sandboxes.declarative_issuers (none by default once the broker trusts two or more issuers). Never carries a credential. Owns exactly one VirtualMachineClaim; a finalizer holds it until the claim and its ClusterStaticEntry are gone. Status mirrors the claim plus whether the entry is set. ADR-0026 (implemented) adds spec.policyRef, the name of a SandboxPolicy in the sandbox's namespace, optional and immutable with the rest of the spec; naming a policy grants nothing in shadow, and under policy.egress: enforce it is what admits the bundle's direct egress (ADR-0030). ADR-0045 adds spec.workload.logs, the requester's opt-in to output capture (boolean, default false, immutable with the rest of the spec). ADR-0069 (accepted and implemented 2026-11-27) adds status.tripwires, every trip event the broker accepted for the claim folded per effect (would_trip, reported, tripped), kind, trap, class, target and source address (at most 16 entries and an overflow count, an entry that ended the claim never evicted, written by compare-and-set apart from the record and ignored by the controller's watch filter; only the broker's ServiceAccount may write the status), and the Tripped condition. A tripped sandbox is Failed, and its record released, so the retention sweep deletes it store.retention_secs later with its status.tripwires and condition (only the audit lines remain); it is never claimed again, as no sandbox is (the acknowledgement annotation of the proposal is struck). ADR-0070 (implemented 2026-11-27) adds the kinds protocol and segment, the source peer and the class to the same entries. Never a bait value, a path or a body; a target the workload or a peer chose is within the host grammar.

nodes.name: Claim Store (the Kubernetes API)
nodes.description: What the broker remembers, in the Kubernetes API (ADR-0034, superseding the database of ADR-0012): the claim record on the AgentSandbox status (status.record, the store's alone: the SPIRE entry id, the node, the bind deadline, the revocation, the policy incarnation and bundle version, the guest's report, the workload's exit, and since ADR-0061 what the guest was handed at its first GET /v1/me (bundle version and digest, routes and rules, egress) and the follow rule's last refusal; the claim UID and the node as labels), the sealed refresh envelope in a Secret owned by the sandbox (key id, nonce, AES-256-GCM ciphertext bound to the sandbox UID; parked by the API, claimed by the reconciler, rotated at every mint, emptied on revocation), attested nodes as SandboxNode resources (EK hash, agent SPIFFE ID, DMI UUID, banned), removed by the watcher once no VM publishes their EK hash (ADR-0039), notaio's version floors as PolicyFloor resources moved by compare-and-set on resourceVersion. The Secrets, the SandboxNode and PolicyFloor resources and the watcher's Lease live in the broker's own namespace, mediatore-system (ADR-0056), each under a Role there (mediatore-sessions, mediatore-store, mediatore-watcher-lease); the ClusterRole holds no verb on the core group and none on the store's two kinds. An envelope is bound to the sandbox's UID and its slot and to no namespace, so a session Secret re-created in another home, without an owner reference, opens for its sandbox (the migration of ADR-0056 decision 7). Since ADR-0057 an update of a claim's record is conditional on the resourceVersion it was read at, a release carries no precondition, the status is written before the Secrets, and the record names its sandbox (sandboxUid, namespace). An ended claim is held by its finalizer for store.retention_secs and then swept, the audit line in the log. In memory under dev_mode only. ADR-0043 decision 4: the sealed envelope in a claim's Secret is deleted, not blanked, when the claim is released, and an envelope for a claim that never binds is deleted when the claim's ttl_seconds has passed counted from creation; the released-claim marker moves to the AgentSandbox status record. ADR-0045 adds the workload output ring beside the session Secrets (data-asset-workload-output). ADR-0069 (accepted and implemented 2026-11-27) adds tripped to the record: the first event that ended the claim (id, the reporter's time and the broker's, kind, trap, class, target, source), written by compare-and-set before the release; a record with tripped set is never restarted and its token is refused. ADR-0070 writes the same field for a claim a protocol class ended (kind protocol, source peer, the class). The claim's trip summary is kept apart from the record (status.tripwires on the cluster, a map in memory under dev_mode) and goes when the record is swept.

nodes.name: OpenBao (transit, PKI)
nodes.description: Encryption as a service for the refresh envelopes (ADR-0015): the transit engine holds the derived sealing key, encrypts and decrypts on request with the binding UID as context, authorises every call by a token it issued to the broker's ServiceAccount (Kubernetes auth, audience openbao) and rotates the key in place. Since ADR-0016 the same engine may hold the RSA key that signs the broker's client assertion for Entra (transit sign, PSS), so the credential that lets mediatore act as itself at Entra never enters the process. Since ADR-0031 its PKI engine is also the SPIRE server's upstream authority: a ten-year root on a dedicated mount signs the server's intermediate CA every ca_ttl (root/sign-intermediate, the one path the server's role may call), so the trust bundle every pool VM and gateway starts from is that root and outlives the server's CA. Reached over TLS the broker and the server verify against a configured CA. In kind: make kind-openbao.

nodes.name: STS Signing Key
nodes.description: EC P-256 private key the STS signs with. A PEM file (sts.signing_key_file, the one shape StsConfig takes); a signer over OpenBao transit is planned, not built. Whoever holds it can mint tokens for any configured audience: guarded asset (threat model TB-1).

nodes.name: Sealing Key
nodes.description: The key that wraps refresh material before it reaches the store (ADR-0012 decision 3). Work shape (ADR-0015): a derived transit key inside OpenBao that never leaves it; the broker holds only a short-lived OpenBao token obtained with its projected ServiceAccount token, and the binding UID is the derivation context. Homelab shape: a 32-byte key from a Secret volume, read into broker memory at start (local sealer).

nodes.name: Kubernetes API Server
nodes.description: Management-cluster API server. mediatore creates and watches AgentSandbox and VirtualMachineClaim through it, and declares SPIRE registration entries as ClusterStaticEntry resources through it. The mediatore-agentsandbox-subject VAP pins spec.subject to the caller except for mediatore's ServiceAccount and listed brokers (ADR-0008); banlieue's claim-subject VAP does the same for claims, with mediatore's ServiceAccount as a listed broker; the mediatore-clusterstaticentry VAP holds whatever the broker's ServiceAccount sends, and from anyone an entry that is the broker's by its name, its managed-by label or a path under /banlieue/, to the two entry shapes, and refuses such an entry from any other sender (ADR-0006, ADR-0056 decision 4); the mediatore-agentsandbox-status VAP admits a status write from the broker alone; the mediatore-clusterspiffeid VAP (ADR-0075) judges every ClusterSPIFFEID create and update from any principal and refuses a spiffeIDTemplate whose path does not begin with a wholly literal segment, or whose first segment is banlieue or gateway, and admits the first segment mediatore only as exactly /mediatore selecting the broker's namespace and ServiceAccount. The four policies that name the broker read its username from one parameter, the key broker of the ConfigMap mediatore-agentsandbox-subject-policy in the broker's namespace, bound with parameterNotFoundAction Deny and failurePolicy Fail: without the ConfigMap they refuse everything they govern, every ClusterSPIFFEID in the cluster included (ADR-0056 decision 4, ADR-0075 decision 6).

nodes.name: banlieue Control Plane
nodes.description: Schedules pool members and binds VirtualMachineClaims to Ready VMs. mediatore consumes its CRDs (banlieue-api types) and never bypasses it; the Kubernetes API is the only interface between the two (banlieue non-negotiable #1, mediatore ADR-0002).

nodes.name: notaio Policy Control Plane
nodes.description: Reviews SandboxPolicy resources and compiles each into a signed bundle: a DSSE envelope over the effective policy (per audience its access, scopes, ttlSeconds, endpoints and rules in the broker's own rule shape; direct egress; the lease's maxDurationSeconds; the policy's namespace, name and uid; a version that only goes up; a notAfter), signed by a key in OpenBao transit that notaio alone can use, published in the policy's namespace as the ConfigMap <policy>-bundle (key bundle.dsse.json, label app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=notaio). mediatore reads what it publishes through the Kubernetes API and nothing else; the signing key never leaves notaio's transit (ADR-0026).

nodes.name: SandboxPolicy bundles (ConfigMaps)
nodes.description: notaio's signed bundles, one ConfigMap per policy in each namespace listed in policy.namespaces. State notaio owns and the broker only reads: the broker's RBAC there is a Role granting get, list and watch on ConfigMaps and nothing else. A bundle is used only once it verifies against the configured keys at the current time and passes notaio's floor rule; one that fails is logged with its reason and changes nothing, an expired one leaves the cache. Under policy.egress: shadow (the default) a bundle is compared with the broker's configuration and reported, never enforced (ADR-0026, roadmap 09, done); under policy.egress: enforce its servable direct egress is served at the gateway (ADR-0030), and a gateway-placed audience must be one the claim's policy admits (ADR-0040). Which namespaces' bundles a sandbox may name is the broker's configuration, policy.sources (ADR-0054), never cluster state: a namespace's own bundles by default, an explicit list otherwise; being read (policy.namespaces) does not make a bundle nameable. ADR-0069 decision 4 (accepted 2026-11-27, not built: the bundle schema is notaio's, so no broker serves a catalogue) is to add a traps section: the deployment's own catalogue of possible tripwires (seed ports, host stems and suffixes, variable names each with a generator, the counts within built-in bounds), widening the public seeds and never narrowing them or carrying a literal value; admission refuses an entry that overlaps a grant of the same policy (P017). Served to the guest on GET /v1/me, never to the proxy.

nodes.name: SandboxAudience bundles (ConfigMaps)
nodes.description: notaio's signed audience bundles (notaio ADR-0020, mediatore ADR-0055): one <audience>-audience ConfigMap per SandboxAudience, the envelope under audience.dsse.json, in the platform audience namespace (platform audiences, visible from every namespace) or a sandbox namespace (team audiences, usable only from that namespace). The kind is the namespace's, never a field of the bundle. Read with the same Role and keys as the policy bundles; verified under the audience payload type, so a policy bundle never verifies as one nor the reverse; a version floor per audience in the store beside the policy floors. Checked again on admission (a team audience's backend is secret or none and never OpenBao, no reserved header, exact DNS endpoints), and a name or endpoint two audiences share is refused for both from every namespace that sees both. Under policy.audience_definitions.mode: shadow they are compared with audiences[] and logged; the file still serves. The credentials they name are read under shadow too (rel-mediatore-audience-secrets, rel-mediatore-openbao-audience-kv) and only the outcome logged; under policy.audience_definitions.mode: bundles the catalog and those credentials serve the API and the watcher in place of audiences[] (ADR-0055, built): a team audience only to claims of its namespace, with 503 audiences_not_synced until the namespaces are listed. ADR-0069 decision 6 (accepted 2026-11-27, not built: the schema is notaio's; audiences[].traps_body in the broker's own file stands in for audiences defined there, and policy.traps enforce is refused at start under bundle-defined audiences) is to add traps.body: skip, which marks an audience that carries the agent's own conversation (a model API) so the egress proxy matches bait in its headers, path and query and not its body.

nodes.name: Policy trust anchor (configured keys)
nodes.description: policy.trusted_keys in the broker's configuration: the Ed25519 public keys, by notaio's key id, that a bundle must be signed with. Configuration, never cluster state, so whoever can write objects in the cluster cannot choose the policy; two versions listed cover a rotation. A key that does not decode to 32 bytes or a duplicate id refuses the start; a missing policy section turns the whole of ADR-0026 off (built: crates/mediatore/src/config.rs).

nodes.name: SPIRE Server (downstream)
nodes.description: The environment-scoped SPIRE server: holds the TPM attestor, the EK trust bundle and the k8s_psat config for this cluster, and issues node identities and workload SVIDs. Its registration entries are rendered by the SPIRE Controller Manager in the same pod over a private Unix socket; no admin API is reachable over the network. mediatore's two entry kinds (/banlieue/node/<ek-hash>, /banlieue/claim/<uid>, ADR-0004) arrive as ClusterStaticEntry resources (ADR-0006). In the enterprise topology it chains to the root via an intermediate CA; in the homelab it is the whole tree (ADR-0005), its CA since ADR-0031 an intermediate signed by OpenBao's PKI engine (deploy/spire-upstream: the vault UpstreamAuthority with a projected ServiceAccount token, audience openbao), so agents anchor on a root that outlives it. The TPM node attestor is spiffe/spire-tpm-plugin as a kustomize component (deploy/spire-tpm: an init container from the digest-pinned image, the checksum in server.conf) and its EK trust bundle is one swtpm local CA issuing certificate per hypervisor host, copied beside the plugin by the init container (ADR-0018).

nodes.name: SPIRE Controller Manager
nodes.description: Runs beside the SPIRE server in the same pod (leader-elected across replicas). Watches ClusterSPIFFEID and ClusterStaticEntry resources and renders them into server registration entries over a private Unix socket; what it renders is bounded at admission, a ClusterSPIFFEID by the mediatore-clusterspiffeid policy (ADR-0075), never by the controller manager itself. The only writer of entries in the cluster; reports status.rendered / masked / set on each resource (ADR-0006).

nodes.name: ClusterStaticEntry resources
nodes.description: Cluster-scoped declarations of mediatore's registration entries: mediatore-node-<node key> (the EK hash, or for an x509pop node the SHA-256 of its agent ID) and mediatore-claim-<uid>, labelled app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=mediatore. Shape enforced at admission by CEL policy: spiffeID under /banlieue/, parentID a tpm agent with the same EK hash or, since ADR-0049 decision 11, an x509pop agent (spire/agent/x509pop/<issuer CN>/<subject CN>), under which the policy cannot hold a node entry's key to its parent, unix selectors only, no admin/downstream/storeSVID. Auditable through the API server audit log and restorable from a cluster backup (ADR-0006).

nodes.name: SPIRE Agent + SPIFFE CSI driver (k8s node)
nodes.description: Per-node DaemonSets from the hardened chart. The agent attests the node with k8s_psat, attests pods through a kubelet whose serving certificate it verifies, and serves the Workload API on a hostPath socket directory. The CSI driver bind-mounts that directory read-only into pods that declare a csi.spiffe.io inline volume, so no workload needs a hostPath. Both are node-level TCB, the same tier as the kubelet (ADR-0007).

nodes.name: SPIRE Root Server (desired state)
nodes.description: Root of the trust domain on the dedicated identity cluster: HA, PostgreSQL-backed, CA keyed through an UpstreamAuthority plugin against an HSM / KMS / corporate PKI. Issues intermediate CAs to downstream servers only; no agent or workload talks to it directly. Elided in the homelab collapse (ADR-0005).

nodes.name: Identity Cluster (desired state)
nodes.description: Dedicated cluster (auth.example.com style) owned by the identity/security team, with its own change control. Hosts only the SPIRE root and its datastore; sandbox-cluster administrators have no access here (ADR-0005).

nodes.name: Management Cluster
nodes.description: The banlieue management cluster: runs mediatore, the downstream SPIRE server with its controller manager, the SPIRE agent and SPIFFE CSI driver DaemonSets, the Kubernetes API and the banlieue controllers. In the homelab this is the single banlieue cluster and the downstream server is the only SPIRE server.

nodes.name: Sandbox VM (pool member)
nodes.description: A banlieue pool member with a fresh vTPM, attested at boot before any claim exists. Boots the sandbox VM image, a Kairos Debian derivative built from this repository (image/Dockerfile, published as ghcr.io/firestoned/mediatore-guest, signed and attested; ADR-0023), an overlay FROM the VM base image (image/base/Dockerfile, ghcr.io/firestoned/mediatore-vm-base: Kairos, Debian 13 and the OS layer it shares with the gateway image, nothing of mediatore's, replaceable by a site's own base; ADR-0067): the one mediatore binary at /usr/bin/mediatore, the SPIRE agent and its TPM attestor plugin in the immutable rootfs, nftables, tpm2-tools, qemu-guest-agent, no sshd or other listener; the agent's configuration and the trust bundle from the deployment's cloud-config layer at every boot, the agent's key on the sealed persistent partition, never in the image. Carries the in-guest agent and, once bound, the jailed workload. Its units start only on the installed disk, and its GuestReady is announced by the in-guest agent after registration (ADR-0019), not by a boot stage. With egress gateways, the pool's cloud-config layer points the agent's server_address and MEDIATORE_URL at a gateway's sandbox address and the control relay's ports, by address, and writes the bootstrap list /etc/mediatore/gateways the guest uses until the broker's gateways arrive (ADR-0027 decisions 3 and 4). With gateways the image also loads inet mediatore_host from the pool's own files (which, for a pool with a gateway-placed audience, include MEDIATORE_INJECT_PORT: each gateway admitted at it for every uid, ADR-0040 decision 13) before the agent and the guest (image/host-table, mediatore-host-nft.service, ADR-0029): the bound on root and every uid, names refused; /etc/mediatore/registries names the mirror and MEDIATORE_REGISTRY_CA its CA. ADR-0063 decision 8 (implemented 2026-11-22): the host table loads before network-pre.target, not only before the agent and the guest; image/host-quiet, run after the table on a pool with gateways only, masks for the boot systemd-timesyncd, systemd-resolved, the apt-daily timers, iscsid, open-iscsi, open-vm-tools and vgauth and removes the base's DHCP catch-all (a direct pool keeps its resolver and DHCP), and the image's datasource stage reads local devices only (cdrom, config-drive, vmware), so nothing on the VM dials out but to the relay's identity-plane legs and the gateways; the registry address and /etc/mediatore/registries leave the host table. ADR-0068 (implemented 2026-11-26): on Azure, read from the DMI chassis asset tag when the table renders, the output chain drops the instance metadata service (169.254.169.254) for every uid ahead of any accept and admits the platform's WireServer (168.63.129.16) to root alone at TCP 80 and 32526 (the ready report of banlieue's helper) and to systemd-networkd's user for the DHCP renewal; off Azure the table is unchanged, and a link-local or platform address in a pool's files is refused everywhere.

nodes.name: SPIRE Agent (in guest)
nodes.description: Attests the node with the vTPM EK certificate and serves the Workload API socket to the guest and to the egress proxy outside the jail; since ADR-0025 the jail has no socket and reaches the proxy alone.

nodes.name: mediatore guest
nodes.description: Root daemon, the guest role of the one mediatore binary (ADR-0014): registers the node (how its agent attested, with the DMI UUID: the EK hash for a TPM node or, under --node-attestation x509pop, the issuer and subject common names of the leaf node-cert wrote, the TPM never opened; ADR-0049 decision 8), then announces GuestReady to the hypervisor over the channel banlieue reads (the /run marker, guestinfo or vsock; ADR-0019), so the pool counts the member only once it is attested and registered; polls GET /v1/me for a bound claim, creates the per-subject user (sb- + 12 hex, ADR-0004), mounts a size-bounded tmpfs at /mnt/sandbox (nosuid, nodev, mode 0711 so the egress proxy reaches its files; ADR-0021 amended) and pulls the claim's workload image from its registry into it as the rootfs (with the operator's credential for that registry when the broker handed one over, used for the pull and kept nowhere; ADR-0022), manifest and layers verified against their digests, the manifest digest logged (ADR-0021), loads the per-claim nftables ruleset keyed by that uid (the broker, the audiences' egress endpoints, DNS; no ruleset, no jail; ADR-0020), bind-mounts the binary at the pinned path read-only into the jail and supervises the nsjail until the deadline, restarting the workload as its restart policy says (ADR-0033: always, on-failure, never) and, when the policy ends the claim, telling the broker how the workload exited (POST /v1/me/exit) so the claim is released, then tears down; what nsjail execs is the binary's jail-exec role, which applies Landlock to itself (the rootfs readable, /work, /tmp and the home writable, TCP connect to the egress proxy's port only, no bind) before the workload's argv runs, and a refusal (exit 125) ends the claim instead of restarting (ADR-0024). Since ADR-0025 it also generates the claim's phantom token, writes the routes GET /v1/me returned to a file of the sandbox user's, starts mediatore egress-proxy as that user outside the jail before the jail, and ends the claim if the proxy exits. crates/mediatore-guest. The ruleset has two shapes since ADR-0028 decision 6 (net::Shape): with gateways, from GET /v1/me or the pool's /etc/mediatore/gateways, the relay, the gateways and the proxy by address and no DNS rule at all, a broker or gateway given by name refusing the claim; without, ADR-0020's list, the broker, the audiences' endpoints resolved at load, the proxy and DNS. The pull trusts the mirror's CA beside the Mozilla roots when told (MEDIATORE_REGISTRY_CA, ADR-0029). Since ADR-0045, for a claim whose requester opted in (workload.logs), it spawns the jail with piped stdout and stderr, redacts every line before it leaves the VM (crates/mediatore-guest/src/redact.rs, logs.rs: the phantom and every secret-bearing environment value, and JWTs, Authorization values and private keys by shape; best effort, not a guarantee), writes the redacted copy to the console, and ships batches to the broker over the node SVID without ever blocking the workload; the last batch is flushed before the exit is reported. ADR-0069 (implemented 2026-11-27): under policy.traps shadow or enforce (served on GET /v1/me, off by default) the guest draws the claim's tripwires at boot from the OS CSPRNG (data-asset-trap-draw): decoy loopback ports, on which nothing listens: the claim's table redirects the sandbox uid's connections to them, and to 169.254.169.254:80 when the metadata decoy is drawn, to one trap listener on a port drawn per claim, which answers as the decoy reached with a plausible first line (nat output rules keyed on that uid; every other uid refused a new connection to a decoy port, every uid refused a direct one to the trap listener, so ADR-0068's drop holds for every other uid), decoy routes and bait credentials it hands to the egress proxy and plants in the jail's environment and the sandbox user's home. On a trip, from the trap listener or from the proxy, it tells the proxy to refuse everything, replaces the sandbox uid's chain with a drop of everything in one nft transaction (cutting the jail and the proxy, never its own path), kills the jail's process tree, flushes the ADR-0045 output and reports POST /v1/me/trip, retried until acknowledged for at most 120 s before its teardown; containment never waits on the broker. Under enforce a run that ends for another reason waits 600 ms for a trip still on its way, which then takes the tripped path. Under enforce a guest that cannot arm its traps starts no jail (GuestReady is announced before any claim exists, so the refusal is at the claim, ADR-0069 decision 5 as amended). The reported ruleset hash leaves the draw out (decision 13 as amended). ADR-0070 decision 4 (implemented 2026-11-27): on a pool VM the guest, root and already driving nft, also reads the named drop counters of the image's host table (pool_inbound, pool_output) and its dynamic sets (inbound_sources, output_ports) every 60 s with nft reset, and reports what moved as kind segment events on POST /v1/me/trip; no rule of the table accepts anything new, and pool_output counts every uid, the sandbox uid's included.

nodes.name: mediatore node-cert (in guest)
nodes.description: ADR-0049 decision 5 (amended 2026-11-24), built (#168, released in v0.4.0): the node-cert role of the one mediatore binary (ADR-0014), on a guest with no vTPM only, in Rust with no subprocess (no openssl, no Python). Runs as the SPIRE agent's own user with no capability. `mediatore node-cert fetch` is a oneshot the agent's unit requires and is ordered after: it generates an EC P-256 key in process (0600 under /run/spire/x509pop/, tmpfs, new each boot, never sent), sends only a PEM CSR to its own host over vsock port 1025, and writes the reply's leaf followed by its chain as one file beside the key, by rename, so the agent never reads a half-written file or a leaf without its chain; no certificate, no agent (fail closed). `mediatore node-cert renew` runs beside the agent and fetches again with the same key at half the remaining life of the certificate on disk; a failed renewal keeps the current files and retries. The reply is size-capped, must parse as PEM certificates, and the leaf's public key must be the guest's own and the leaf valid now; the subject is the host's choice (the VM's UID) and is not checked here. The lifetime is the host's (bounded 5 min to 7 days by banlieue's installer); backoff stays under the host signer's per-guest rate limit. Never logs the key, the CSR or a certificate body: serial, issuer and notAfter only. crates/mediatore-guest/src/nodecert.rs; the units image/systemd/mediatore-node-cert.service and mediatore-node-cert-renew.service (no capability, AF_VSOCK and AF_UNIX only), pulled in only by the drop-in a pool without a vTPM installs. Proven against banlieue's real signer and a real SPIRE server and agent on the build host (#168); not yet on a guest booted on a Cloud Hypervisor or Firecracker host end to end through the broker.

nodes.name: Jailed Workload
nodes.description: Runs under nsjail as the per-subject user in a read-only rootfs unpacked from the claim's image onto a per-claim tmpfs (ADR-0021), with only the binary mounted in and /work writable, in the VM's network namespace behind an nftables chain keyed by its uid (ADR-0020); and under Landlock, applied by its own process before the first instruction of the workload (mediatore jail-exec, ADR-0024): writes only to /work, /tmp and the home whatever the image's file modes say, TCP connect to the egress proxy's loopback port and no other, no TCP bind, signals and abstract sockets scoped to the jail, inherited by every child. And a third layer in the same process (ADR-0051, crates/mediatore-guest/src/seccomp.rs): a seccomp filter applied after Landlock that refuses every socket family but AF_UNIX, AF_INET and AF_INET6, any inet socket that is not a stream, and io_uring, so a vsock, a UDP socket or an io_uring socket operation no longer depends on the nftables chain or on a dropped capability. Holds no credential: since ADR-0025 the Workload API socket is not mounted, the broker is unreachable, and the jail's environment carries MEDIATORE_EGRESS_PROXY (http://127.0.0.1:3128) and MEDIATORE_TOKEN, a phantom the proxy swaps for the real token on the way out. The binary stays mounted read-only for jail-exec (ADR-0014, ADR-0024). ADR-0069 (implemented 2026-11-27): under policy.traps shadow or enforce the jail's environment and the sandbox user's home (never /work) also carry bait the workload cannot tell from real: credentials in their providers' shapes, variables pointing at decoy routes on the proxy, and decoy services on loopback; the home is then a bind mount the guest planted, kept across the workload's restarts within the claim. Reading them trips nothing; connecting to a decoy, naming a decoy route or sending a bait value does.

nodes.name: mediatore egress-proxy
nodes.description: The egress-proxy role of the one binary (ADR-0025), one process per claim started by the guest as the sandbox user outside the jail, in the VM's namespace and filesystem. A reverse proxy on 127.0.0.1:3128: the workload calls /<host>[:<port>]/<path> with the phantom token, the proxy checks the host against the claim's routes (one per audience and egress endpoint, and under policy.egress enforce one per direct egress entry of the claim's bundle the gateway serves, from GET /v1/me) and the method and path against the route's rules (nono's endpoint_rules shape: method or *, a path glob with * one segment and ** any), swaps the phantom for a token for the route's audience fetched over the claim SVID at POST /v1/token and cached until shortly before its expiry, or on a route with credential none (a bundle's direct entry, an audience via: none; ADR-0025 decision 8) drops the phantom and forwards bare; for an audience via: secret (ADR-0032) the credential is the operator's, placed in the header the broker named (Authorization as a bearer, or x-api-key and the like) with the extra headers beside it, the phantom recognised in that header too and every owned header stripped on every route; and forwards over TLS 1.3 to the Mozilla roots, or to the CA the route carries for an audience on a private PKI (audiences[].ca_file, ADR-0025 decision 7). No TLS interception. A request with no Authorization header is forwarded bare, one with a foreign bearer is 401 on every route, one outside the rules 403, one to a host not in the routes 404. In an environment with egress gateways (the gateways list on GET /v1/me, ADR-0028 decision 6) the upstream is not dialled directly: the proxy's dialer is the forwarder of ADR-0028 decision 3, placed in this process by ADR-0027 decision 8 (crates/mediatore-guest/src/forward.rs): TLS 1.3 to a gateway on the sandbox leg's configuration presenting the claim SVID and verifying spiffe://<td>/gateway, CONNECT host:port, the upstream's TLS inside the tunnel; the list walked from a random start per connection, a connect or handshake failure moving to the next (decision 7), a gateway's refusal final (502 gateway_refused at the workload, the authorizer's code in the log; 502 gateway_unreachable when none carried it). The only process that ever holds a downstream token or the claim SVID; the uid-keyed table drops packets to its port from any other uid, and a proxy that exits ends the claim. crates/mediatore-guest/src/egress.rs. ADR-0040: on a route with credential: gateway the proxy never fetches a token; it sends the request in origin form to the gateway's inject port over the claim-SVID mutual TLS and the gateway places the credential. ADR-0069 (implemented 2026-11-27): carries the drawn decoy routes (hosts that are no audience) and the bait values, handed by the guest over a root-owned unix socket the jail cannot reach. Every request is checked before anything is forwarded: the method, header names and values, path and query whole before the tunnel opens; the body streamed through a multi-pattern matcher (each bait raw, percent-encoded and base64 at three alignments) that holds back the longest pattern, so a complete bait value never leaves the VM; an encoded body decoded for the matcher. A request naming a decoy route or carrying bait is 403 trap, the upstream stream is reset, nothing more is forwarded for the claim, and the guest is told; once the guest says it decided a trip of its own, every request is 403 trap. An audience marked audiences[].traps_body: skip in the broker's configuration (a model API, the agent's own conversation) is matched on headers, path and query only. A body over the expansion bound or undecodable is refused under enforce (413, 400) and forwarded under shadow, and ends nothing. The proxy never sees a trap catalogue, only the draw. Since ADR-0049 decision 12 (built 2026-11-27) the proxy's first act, before it reads or binds anything, is a seccomp address-family filter on all its threads that leaves it unix and inet sockets and no other kind (seccomp::restrict_families, the family half of ADR-0051's policy), proven by asking for a netlink and a vsock socket; it does not start unless both are refused.

nodes.name: Egress gateway (Envoy + mediatore gateway, with the control relay beside them)
nodes.description: The egress gateway of ADR-0028 on each of banlieue's three proxy VMs per environment (banlieue ADR-0109), built as image content (image/gateway/, an overlay FROM the same VM base image as the sandbox image, ADR-0067, published as ghcr.io/firestoned/mediatore-gateway, signed and attested; the VMs, the two-interface class and the entries in deploy/gateway/). The data plane: Envoy on the sandbox address, mutual TLS 1.3 with X25519MLKEM768 offered first, its own identity spiffe://<td>/gateway over SDS from the local SPIRE agent (the VM attests with its vTPM like a pool member; ClusterStaticEntry objects per VM applied by the platform team, one per user: unix:user:envoy and, with inject, unix:user:envoy-inject for spiffe://<td>/gateway, and unix:user:mediatore-gateway for the authorizer's own identity spiffe://<td>/gateway/authorizer, ADR-0053, its client identity to the broker, selected by path and required at start; an admission policy pins the two shapes, deploy/base/admission/clusterstaticentry-gateway.yaml; the host table's output chain, keyed on the socket's owner, admits the broker's address to the authorizer's and the relay's users alone and refuses both Envoys loopback, link-local, the control-plane addresses and IPv6, image/gateway/nftables.conf.in), every peer required to be a claim of the trust domain before any filter runs, CONNECT the only route, each tunnel checked with the authorizer beside it, mediatore gateway (crates/mediatore-gateway: Envoy's own Check call over gRPC, on a unix socket the tunnel Envoy's group alone reaches by default since 2026-11-26, loopback TCP only where an env file asks for it; the peer from the verified certificate, the method and the authority; OK or PERMISSION_DENIED with a stable code from a bounded cache of one allowlist per claim, fresh 30 s, stale for 300 s more while the broker is unreachable, never past the claim's deadline, dropped on the broker's 404, least recently used evicted past 4096 claims, one ask per claim at a time, deny on no answer), the authority resolved and dialled by Envoy from the egress address, one access-log line per tunnel keyed by the peer's SPIFFE ID, no admin interface, no interception. The host: forwarding off, an nftables table with default-drop input admitting the data port and the relay ports on the sandbox interface only, nothing new on egress, both Envoys as their own users with no capability and a read-only root (ADR-0028 decision 8, ADR-0027 decision 5). The bootstrap the kind tier proves is the image's template rendered with the tier's values (make kind-e2e-gateway, make gateway-render-check). The image is built and checked (image/gateway/check.sh) and runs live on the gateway VMs since 2026-11-05 (roadmap 10). ADR-0040 (implemented): where an audience is declared inject: gateway the authorizer also answers a second question on a second unix socket, for envoy-inject (a third Envoy process beside the data plane and the relay), obtains the credential from the broker (POST /v1/gateway/claims/{uid}/credential) and returns it only to that Envoy in the check response; the data-plane socket never returns one. ADR-0068 (implemented 2026-11-26): ahead of every user's row the host table's output chain drops the instance metadata service for every user, root included, and keeps Azure's WireServer to root at TCP 80 and 32526 and to systemd-networkd's DHCP renewal, its port 53 left to the per-user rows as any resolver. ADR-0070 decision 4 (implemented 2026-11-27): each dropping rule of the host table gains a named counter (gateway_port on the input drop, gateway_output per user on the output drops) and the input drop a dynamic set of source addresses with a timeout; no rule accepts anything new. A oneshot unit under a 30 s timer, mediatore gateway-probes, as its own user mediatore-probes holding CAP_NET_ADMIN alone with no address family but netlink and no listener, reads and resets the counters and writes a summary to its own directory, which the authorizer reads and cannot write; the authorizer adds it to its next decisions batch as probes and gains no capability.

nodes.name: Control relay (Envoy, no identity)
nodes.description: ADR-0027's control plane on each gateway VM: a second Envoy, its own systemd unit and user (envoy-relay, image/gateway/systemd/envoy-relay.service), with no SPIRE socket (InaccessiblePaths=/run/spire), no SVID and no credential of any kind. Four tcp_proxy listeners on the sandbox address, 3129 to the SPIRE server's attestation port, 3130 to the broker's sandbox listener, 3131 (ADR-0037) to the SPIRE servers' bundle endpoint and 3132 (ADR-0038) to the operator's registry, each a fixed upstream by address from the deployment's env file (image/gateway/envoy/relay.yaml.in): no CONNECT, no authority from the client, no name resolution for the sandbox. It carries the pool VM's bootstrap connections as ciphertext, the TLS end to end between the agent and the server, between the node or the claim and the broker, between the boot-time bundle fetch and the bundle endpoint (its web PKI certificate, checked by the member against the endpoint's hostname), and between the guest's image pull and the registry (the registry's own certificate, checked against its own name; admitted by the host table to uid 0 alone, never in the jail's table), and sees only metadata, which it logs one line per connection (source, upstream, bytes each way, duration). The host table bounds each sandbox source's new relay connections (ct count over RELAY_CAP in a dynamic set, ADR-0027 decision 5), since the relay has no identity to rate-limit by. It is the only way a pool VM reaches the identity plane: the segment has no route and no resolver. ADR-0063 (2026-11-22) removed the fourth leg, 3132 to the registry; the relay has three, all to the identity plane.

nodes.name: Downstream APIs
nodes.description: Services the sandbox may call on the user's behalf: Entra-protected APIs (OBO tokens) or JWKS-validating services (STS tokens with the act claim). Each validates audience and can audit 'broker on behalf of user'.

nodes.name: Workload Image Registry
nodes.description: The OCI registry the claim's workload.image names. The guest's puller verifies every blob against its digest and logs the manifest digest that ran; a tag is the registry's word, a digest pin is the requester's (ADR-0021). Trusted for availability, not for content. Without egress gateways the guest pulls from it directly over HTTPS, anonymously or with the operator's credential from the broker's config (ADR-0022). With gateways (ADR-0063, implemented 2026-11-22) a registry is a SandboxAudience marked role: registry in a signed bundle, a platform audience a namespace's policy grants or a team audience locked to its namespace (ADR-0055), pull-only; the broker refuses a claim whose image is on a registry its namespace was not granted (400 registry_not_granted), and every pull reaches it through the claim's egress proxy and a gateway, a tunnel on the data port (rel-gateway-registry) or the inject Envoy with a placed credential (rel-envoy-inject-registry, ADR-0043). The broker-global registries[] and its reach (segment, relay; ADR-0029, ADR-0038) are refused with gateways.

nodes.name: Sandbox Network Segment
nodes.description: Pool members' network, layer 2 only (banlieue ADR-0109): no route anywhere and no resolver. A member reaches exactly the three gateways' sandbox addresses: the data plane (TCP 8443, mutual TLS with the claim SVID, CONNECT to the claim's allowlist) and the control relay (TCP 3129 to the SPIRE server, 3130 to the broker, 3131 to the bundle endpoint, ADR-0037, and 3132 to the operator's registry for root's pull alone, ADR-0038; the TLS inside end to end). The SPIRE server, the broker's sandbox listener, the workload image registry and the downstream APIs are reached through the gateways and never directly; from inside the jail the sandbox uid reaches the egress proxy on loopback alone, and the proxy's own sockets the relay and the gateways by address (ADR-0020 as amended by ADR-0028 decision 6 and ADR-0027 decision 6). Nothing inbound to a VM. In an environment without gateways yet, the older shape: the broker, the audiences' egress endpoints and the resolvers. The workload image registry a gateway-era pool pulls from is on this segment too, a registry or pull-through mirror at layer 2 (ADR-0029 decision 1): a public registry is unreachable by construction. Every uid on a member is bounded by the image's host table, input and forward dropped, output to the gateways' two planes and the segment's registries alone (ADR-0029 decision 3).

nodes.name: envoy-inject (credential placement Envoy, ADR-0040)
nodes.description: ADR-0040's third Envoy on each gateway VM, only where an audience is declared inject: gateway: its own systemd unit and static user (envoy-inject), no admin interface, its own SPIRE entry for the gateway SPIFFE ID (unix:user:envoy-inject, one entry per user). One listener on the sandbox address and its own port (INJECT_PORT, admitted by the gateway's nftables table to the sandbox range under the per-source cap): mutual TLS 1.3 with the claim SAN prefix required, HTTP/1.1, no CONNECT route, no dynamic forward proxy. A route matches the request's :authority exactly against the one upstream the env file names (INJECT_HOST, INJECT_UPSTREAM_PORT, INJECT_DOMAIN; a second upstream is a second virtual host and cluster in the template, a reviewed change like a relay leg, never a parameter) and goes to a static cluster with TLS origination (SNI the host; system roots, or a PEM for a private PKI); a host not in the list has no route (404). ext_authz on the listener asks the authorizer on inject/inject.sock (group envoy-inject) with context_extensions mode inject; the authorizer alone writes the credential header (OVERWRITE_IF_EXISTS_OR_ADD) and removes any a client sent, so no route, virtual-host or listener-level header rule may name the credential header (Envoy applies those after ext_authz; shown on 1.40.2, TESTING.md T-61). Paths are normalised before the authorizer's rules see them (normalize_path, merge_slashes, an escaped slash rejected). The per-claim limit of ADR-0040 decision 5 is not built (a marked placeholder in the template): until it is, the host table's per-source connection cap bounds a sandbox's connections to the port. The credential is in a request's headers for at most the 300 second cap and is never logged (access log without headers, info level, suppress_envoy_headers). The data-plane Envoy and the relay never hold a credential: this is the only Envoy that does. Without a gateway-placed audience it is not started.

nodes.name: The requester's saved credential (OS credential store)
nodes.description: ADR-0041 decision 5, amended by ADR-0043 decision 5: one item per audience in the requester's own OS credential store (the macOS Keychain; service mediatore, account the audience), holding the user name and secret and the time they were saved, created only on an explicit yes (the default is no). Its age limit is the least of six hours and the claim's TTL: an item older than that is deleted and refused, and mediatore logout --audience deletes it. Read and written by the CLI on the requester's machine; never sent anywhere but in the claim body (ADR-0041 decision 3), and the requester's OS decides which other programs may read it. Other platforms have no store source. Status: the six-hour bound is live; the claim-TTL bound (ADR-0043 decision 5) is built and unit-tested, not yet run live.

nodes.name: Workload output (the Secret ring)
nodes.description: ADR-0045: the redacted stdout and stderr of a sandbox whose requester opted in (workload.logs: true), as the broker keeps it: a ring of Secrets in the broker's own namespace, mediatore-logs-<claim uid>-<segment>, 64 KiB of record text per segment, labelled mediatore.io/logs=segment with the claim and sandbox UIDs, owned by the AgentSandbox when it shares the namespace, capped at logs.max_bytes per claim (default 1 MiB, ceiling 4 MiB; the oldest segment dropped and the dropped bytes counted), swept by the leader's resync logs.retention_secs after the claim ended (default: store.retention_secs). Since ADR-0052 each segment's entries are sealed per ingested batch with the broker's OpenBao transit key (the same mount, key and role as the sessions, a separate derivation context bound to the claim UID and the output's purpose): one blob per line, with only the sequence range, the record text byte count and the key id in clear, the segment marked mediatore.io/seal=v1; at most 64 KiB of record text per blob, so a maximum batch is at most 5 transit calls. Each stored unit, once opened, is a LogRecord {seq, stream, ts, text} or a LogGap {lost_stdout, lost_stderr, unreadable}. Readable through the broker by the claim's owner alone (the same subject check as GET /v1/claims/{name}); an unreachable sealer is a 503 on ingest and on read and never a plaintext fallback, a blob that does not open for the claim or a segment without the seal marker is served as an unreadable gap and never as output, and logs.enabled without store.sealing refuses to start. A cluster administrator reading the Secrets directly sees ciphertext; acting as the broker at OpenBao is what decrypts (threat model R-39, narrowed). Redaction happened in the VM and is best effort (R-38): the ring is a Secret, not a ConfigMap, because it may hold what redaction missed. In memory under dev_mode with the same cap, cursor and sweep rules (LogRing, crates/mediatore-store). Nothing is stored for a sandbox that did not opt in or on a broker with logs.enabled false.

nodes.name: Per-host signing CA bundle (x509pop trust anchors, ADR-0049)
nodes.description: ADR-0049, built 2026-11-27 as the kustomize component deploy/spire-x509pop: ConfigMap spire-x509pop-host-cas, one PEM per host, joined into one file by an init container and read when the server starts (the hosts' CAs and signer are built in banlieue, ADR-0146). The x509pop NodeAttestor's ca_bundle_path on the SPIRE server: one CA certificate per host whose guests have no vTPM, each created at the host's install and held (key included) only by that host's provider; the certificate is public and an operator adds it to the bundle when onboarding the host, never discovered from the host. Controls: (1) every CA in the bundle must have a UNIQUE, operator-chosen common name and be a CA with a path length of zero, because the agent ID is issuer-qualified and a duplicate, or a CA that can sign a CA, removes the confinement; nothing in mediatore reads a live server's bundle to check either. The check is a command, mediatore x509pop-bundle check <file>..., which applies those rules to the bundle's files (mediatore-spire refuse_duplicate_common_names, its one caller) and exits non-zero naming the certificate: the operator runs it before the ConfigMap is applied, every time it changes, and the kind tier runs it on the server's real ConfigMap and on two bundles it must refuse (make kind-e2e-x509pop); it is enforced on no server (threat model R-73), while the watcher holds the host CA it reads from a Provider to the path length on every declaration (host_ca_common_name); (2) the server's agent_path_template is /x509pop/{{ .Issuer.CommonName }}/{{ .Subject.CommonName }}, giving the agent ID spiffe://<td>/spire/agent/x509pop/<issuer CN>/<subject CN>, stable across certificate renewal and declarable before the guest boots, with both common names restricted to the path-segment alphabet (mediatore-spire x509pop_agent_id); (3) the host's signer ignores the CSR subject and sets the subject CN to the VM's UID, basicConstraints CA:FALSE (the server does not enforce it) and keyUsage digitalSignature (the server requires it), with a bounded validity; (4) a compromised host can speak only for its own guests, under its own CA's name; (5) retiring a CA revokes every identity it signed at the agents' next re-attestation. No SPIRE admin identity and no join token: mediatore still only declares ClusterStaticEntry (ADR-0006). The TPM attestor and its EK CA bundle (ADR-0018) are unchanged and stay the attestor of every guest with a vTPM.

nodes.name: The claim's tripwire draw (ADR-0069)
nodes.description: ADR-0069 decision 3 (implemented 2026-11-27, crates/mediatore-guest/src/draw.rs): which decoy ports, decoy routes and bait credentials a claim's sandbox carries, how many of each, and every bait value, drawn by the guest at boot from the OS CSPRNG out of public seeds, generated entries, entries derived from the claim's real routes and the deployment's catalogue in the policy bundle; a drawn entry that collides with anything real is redrawn. Held in the guest's memory and handed to the egress proxy; never in the image, the bundle, the record, GET /v1/me or a log at info, and gone with the VM. Nothing of it leaves the VM except the one trap a trip report names. The secret is the draw, never the method: the catalogues and the code are public. No broker serves a deployment catalogue yet: the bundle's traps section is notaio's schema (decision 4 as amended), so a draw is made from the seeds, the generated and the derived entries.

relationships.description: The mediatore system is one binary composed of the two API surfaces, the claim watcher and the STS; the claim store and the STS signing key are the state it guards, with the configured policy keys the trust anchor for notaio's bundles (ADR-0026).

Everything identity-bearing on a pool member: the SPIRE agent (node identity), the in-guest agent (subject plumbing), the egress proxy (claim identity, the tokens) and the jailed workload (a phantom token and one loopback route). Since ADR-0069 (implemented 2026-11-27) also the claim's tripwire draw, held by the guest and the proxy.

Pool members live on the layer 2 sandbox segment; the gateways and their control relay have their sandbox interface on it and their egress interface on a routable network (banlieue ADR-0109 decision 4).

Everything control-plane-side shares the management cluster; the SPIRE downstream server, its controller manager and the per-node agent and CSI driver are scoped to it so entry rendering, k8s_psat validation and pod attestation stay per-environment.
The root SPIRE server lives alone on the identity cluster; the root signing key never resides where sandboxes are administered.

Nested SPIRE: the downstream server obtains its intermediate CA from the root and chains every SVID it issues to the one trust domain. Revoking the intermediate cuts an entire environment off from above. Absent in the homelab collapse (ADR-0005).
The user logs in at the IdP (PKCE via mediatore login or az login) and receives a token whose audience is mediatore. The user's token is only ever presented to mediatore, never to the VM.

POST /v1/claims with the IdP bearer token creates an AgentSandbox with the token's subject (ADR-0008); GET answers from its status, DELETE deletes it. Subject equality is enforced on read and delete, and the caller must be in the claim's namespace's groups for create, read and delete alike (ADR-0046): a person who left the group can no longer read or delete through the broker, and a cluster administrator's kubectl delete is the break-glass path. The request may name a namespace (ClaimRequest.namespace, ClaimResponse.namespace). For a via: delegated audience (ADR-0035) the request carries the caller's own credential for it (the CLI reads Claude Code's session, a variable or a file), sealed with the AgentSandbox UID into a Secret of its own beside the session's and opened only at POST /v1/token for the proxy; a claim naming such an audience without it is refused. For a session issuer the request also carries the caller's refresh token (mediatore login, PKCE as client mediatore; ADR-0013), which is sealed with the AgentSandbox UID into a sessions row before the response and follows the claim into its record; it never touches the resource. Since ADR-0045, GET /v1/claims/{name}/logs?follow=&since=&tail= streams the stored output of a claim created with workload.logs: true as NDJSON (a header with the dropped byte count and the phase, the records and gaps in sequence, an end line) to the claim's owner under the same subject and namespace checks, 501 when the broker's logs section is off, 503 when the store cannot be read; a follower is re-read when a batch for its claim is stored through this replica and at least every two seconds, with an empty keepalive line every fifteen; every read is one audit line with the claim UID and subject and never the content. A POST /v1/claims with workload.logs: true on a broker with logs.enabled false is refused 501 before anything is created.

JWKS discovery and signature validation for incoming tokens; for a session issuer (ADR-0013, built), a refresh_token grant before every token issue, as mediatore's own public client: the fresh ID token is validated like a login (group gate included), the rotated refresh token re-sealed into the record, and invalid_grant releases the claim at once. For an Entra issuer (ADR-0016, built): the On-Behalf-Of exchange of the caller's access token at claim creation (offline_access, the first entra-obo audience or mediatore's own resource), mediatore authenticating with a PS256 client assertion signed by a key file, by OpenBao transit, or presented as a projected ServiceAccount token under workload identity federation; before every issue a refresh_token grant naming the audience's resource, a token for mediatore itself validated like a login for an sts audience, Entra's token handed to the workload as is for an entra-obo audience. The user's original token is discarded after validation.

Creates the AgentSandbox, in the namespace the broker resolved from the token's groups and its namespace map (ADR-0046; the ServiceAccount can create in all of them, so the map is the control on the broker's front door and does not govern the declarative path), with spec.subject from the validated token (ADR-0008) and the annotation mediatore.io/front-door: api (ADR-0072), which the broker proves at start the subject policy reserves to it by a dry-run create the policy must refuse; the reconciler, not the user API, creates the VirtualMachineClaim. The mediatore ServiceAccount is exempt from the caller-equals-subject check of the agentsandbox-subject policy because it acts for subjects it has validated tokens for, and is listed as a broker in banlieue's claim-subject policy.

Watches VirtualMachineClaim (label app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=mediatore) for Bound / Releasing / Failed / deletion and VirtualMachine (banlieue.io/pool) for a published vTPM endorsement certificate; binds by the EK hash the claim mirrors, fails an unresolved bind after 60 s by deleting the claim, declares node entries from members (ADR-0011). Since ADR-0049, and only while watcher.x509pop_pools is not empty, it also reads the machine every Bound claim names (status.virtualMachineRef), whose pool label says which attestor applies, and, for the machines of the listed pools and for no other, the Providers (list on providers and no other verb), listed cluster-wide once per pass: a machine's Provider is the one of that name in the machine's namespace, or in watcher.provider_namespace when that namespace holds none, read for the host CA asserted inline (spec.attestation.hostCa.inline; a configMapRef or secretRef is refused, not followed), and such a claim is bound by the key of its x509pop agent ID, never by its EK. The rival rule: when two Providers, in any namespaces, assert different certificates under one common name, no machine of either gets an entry and their claims fail naming both; the same certificate on two Providers is one CA. Runs on the replica holding the coordination.k8s.io Lease mediatore-watcher.

Watches AgentSandbox and creates, owns and deletes its one VirtualMachineClaim through the Kubernetes API with the broker ServiceAccount (ADR-0008, built). RBAC: get/list/watch/patch/create/delete on agentsandboxes, patch on agentsandboxes/status and update on agentsandboxes/finalizers; create/delete/get/list/watch on virtualmachineclaims. Never patches a pool member: binding stays in banlieue's claim controller.

Collects the SandboxNode of a VM that no longer exists (ADR-0039, built): once per resync, on the replica holding the Lease, lists the pool member VirtualMachines (get/list/watch on virtualmachines, already granted) and deletes a SandboxNode whose node key no VM gives: the EK hash of its certificate, or for a machine of a pool listed as x509pop the key of its agent ID (delete on sandboxnodes, already granted). Never a banned node, a node younger than store.node_grace_secs (600 s by default), a node an unended claim is bound to, or more than 20 per pass; an empty VM list is not believed while a node is young or a claim is active; a failed listing removes nothing. For the pools listed as x509pop there is one more hold (ADR-0049 decision 10): a pass collects no x509pop node and no x509pop node entry while a listed machine's Provider is not found, whatever the machine's age, or while a listed machine with no attestationSubject or no placement yet is young, its creationTimestamp less than store.node_grace_secs ago (a machine with no creation timestamp is not young). Past that grace such a machine holds nothing. The hold without a bound is a machine whose published placement names a Provider that does not exist (threat model R-26).
An AgentSandbox is the sandbox user's request, attributed to them by admission; the claim, entry and tokens all derive from it.
banlieue's claim controller binds Ready pool members to claims and destroys members on release; mediatore only observes the results. CRDs are the entire interface.

Declares the claim entry (parent = the bound VM's tpm agent ID, selector unix:user:sb-<hash>) as a ClusterStaticEntry on Bound and deletes it on release, through the Kubernetes API with the broker ServiceAccount. RBAC: create/delete/get/list/watch on clusterstaticentries only; the mediatore-clusterstaticentry admission policy rejects any other shape and any other sender of an entry that looks like the broker's. Before it serves, and again at each resync on the replica holding the Lease, the broker proves the policy binds it with a server-side dry run of an entry the policy must refuse (ADR-0056 decision 5): an admitted probe, a refusal that is not the policy's, a policy that does not name it or cannot read its parameter, and no answer are each a start error, and at a resync they stop new entries from being declared (the gate in front of the entry manager) while releasing nothing. Waits for status.set. No gRPC, no admin SVID (ADR-0006).

notaio writes each policy's bundle ConfigMap in the policy's namespace and keeps it current: a new version on every change, re-signed on a key rotation (ADR-0026); and each SandboxAudience's bundle ConfigMap in the audience's namespace, once its platform audience namespace is set (notaio ADR-0020, mediatore ADR-0055). mediatore never calls notaio; the ConfigMap is the whole interface.

The bundle reflector (ADR-0026 decision 3, implemented): a watch on ConfigMaps labelled app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=notaio in each namespace of policy.namespaces, with a Role per namespace granting get, list and watch on ConfigMaps and nothing else. A ConfigMap without bundle.dsse.json, or whose envelope does not parse, is logged and ignored. The condition the comparison writes goes through rel-watcher-agentsandboxes, on agentsandboxes/status.

The audience reflector (ADR-0055 decision 1, built for shadow): a watch on ConfigMaps labelled app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=notaio in the platform audience namespace and every sandbox namespace, under the policy bundles' Role (get, list and watch on ConfigMaps only). A ConfigMap without audience.dsse.json is a policy bundle or not notaio's and is skipped. Every replica runs it, outside the Lease; the SandboxAudience CRD is never read. ADR-0063: an audience marked role: registry is a registry the namespace may pull from, pull-only.

A team audience's credential, or a platform audience's secretRef (ADR-0055 decision 5, built; read and logged under shadow, served under bundles): get on one named Secret in the audience's own namespace, polled every credential_refresh_secs, through a Role with resourceNames per namespace (deploy/audience-credentials), created at onboarding and never by the broker. No list, no watch, no write.
The policy and audience bundles are notaio's state; mediatore holds a verified copy in memory and the floors in its store.
Watches ClusterSPIFFEID and ClusterStaticEntry resources and reports rendering status on them.

Unix domain socket, not a network protocol (CALM's protocol enum has no value for it). Renders declared resources into registration entries over the server's private Unix socket inside the pod. The admin API is never exposed on the network.

Unix domain socket, not a network protocol (CALM's protocol enum has no value for it). The broker pod fetches spiffe://<td>/mediatore and the trust-domain bundle from the node's SPIRE agent over the Workload API socket, mounted read-only by the SPIFFE CSI driver (no hostPath). SVID and key stay in process memory and rotate on the stream (ADR-0007).
k8s_psat node attestation with a projected, audience-bound ServiceAccount token, then SVID fetching for attested pods.

TPM node attestation at boot (EK certificate + credential activation), then SVID rotation. Claim-independent: a warm member is attested before any claim exists. With egress gateways the agent's server_address is a gateway's sandbox address and the relay's SPIRE port (ADR-0027 decision 3): the attestation's TLS is end to end, the relay sees ciphertext. One address, so the agent fails over between gateways only when it restarts (ADR-0027's open item).

POST /v1/nodes (the attestation + DMI UUID + hostname) over the node SVID at boot: a top-level ek_hash for a TPM node, as every guest up to v0.4.0 sent, or attestation {kind: x509pop, issuer_cn, subject_cn}; the broker derives the node key and the agent ID from it with the functions the watcher declares node entries with, requires the peer's SPIFFE ID to be banlieue/node/<that key> (403 otherwise) and refuses an unknown kind or field with 400 invalid_attestation (ADR-0049 decision 8); then polls GET /v1/me until a claim is bound and the subject comes back. Since ADR-0022 the answer to GET /v1/me includes the pull credential for the claim's image registry when the operator configured one. Since ADR-0025 it carries the proxy's routes, and since ADR-0025 decision 8 (2026-11-08) a route may carry credential none: one per served direct egress entry of the claim's bundle under policy.egress enforce, with no audience, and the routes of an audience via: none. Since ADR-0028 decision 6 the answer also carries gateways, the environment's egress gateways in the broker's order, for the forwarder and the ruleset; empty until the gateways exist. With egress gateways the connection itself runs through a gateway's control relay (ADR-0027 decision 3), the node SVID's mutual TLS end to end inside it, and the guest falls back to the pool's bootstrap list /etc/mediatore/gateways when the answer lists none (decision 4). Once the image is pulled and the tables are loaded, before the jail, the guest POSTs /v1/me/report over the same identity: the manifest digest, the sandbox ruleset's hash and the host table as nft lists it, hashed, or its absence (ADR-0029 decision 5); the broker keeps it on the claim's record (logged when the claim is swept), and GET /v1/claims/{name} shows it. Since ADR-0045, when GET /v1/me says workload.logs the guest also POSTs /v1/me/logs over the node SVID: batches of the jailed workload's stdout and stderr lines, redacted in the VM (the phantom and every secret-bearing environment value literally and in their base64 and percent-encoded forms; JWTs, Authorization values and private-key PEM blocks by shape), on the leading edge (at once after a quiet half second, otherwise every half second, or at 32 KiB; a line that has not ended after 150 ms of silence as a partial record, less the end the redactor holds back), with a per-claim sequence number the broker uses to accept a retried batch idempotently and per-stream dropped byte counts when the guest's 1 MiB queue overflowed; the workload never waits for the broker, a 429 is honoured, a 501 or 404 stops shipping for the claim and keeps the console copy, and the last batch is flushed, bounded to five seconds, before POST /v1/me/exit. The broker accepts a batch from the claim's node alone, re-validates its shape and size (400, 413), rate-limits it to two per second (429), refuses one for a claim that did not opt in (400 logs_not_requested), and answers 501 with logs.enabled off. Since ADR-0069 (amended 2026-11-27) a claim a tripwire ended still has its batches taken from the node it was bound to for 60 s after the trip, so its final line reaches the owner. Since ADR-0069 (implemented 2026-11-27) GET /v1/me also serves policy.traps (off, shadow, enforce), read by the guest outside the jail; a trip is reported on its own route (rel-guest-agent-trip). ADR-0069: under policy.traps shadow or enforce the answer to GET /v1/me carries traps (the mode, what each denied class does; no catalogue until notaio's bundle carries one) and traps_body on each route (skip on an audience marked audiences[].traps_body: skip in the broker's configuration). ADR-0070 decision 3 (implemented 2026-11-27): the broker classifies the refusals it already gives a node identity on this listener, changing no answer: foreign_route (a node on POST /v1/token or a gateway route), unknown_route (a path the router does not serve), no_record (a node identity whose EK hash is not registered, on any route but POST /v1/nodes). A node's classes are recorded; the claim bound to it, if any, is ended only where the class is set to trip.
