After POST /v1/nodes is accepted, the installed-guest announcement banlieue ADR-0043 defines, on the channel its provider reads: /run/banlieue/phase (libvirt, through qemu-guest-agent), guestinfo.banlieue.phase (vSphere), phase=installed over vsock (Cloud Hypervisor). Liveness only; mediatore reads it nowhere (ADR-0019).

The in-guest agent, as root and before the ruleset is loaded, pulls the claim's workload image: the manifest (an index resolved to linux/<arch>) and the layers, each verified against its digest, applied in order with whiteouts into the rootfs on the per-claim tmpfs; nothing escapes the rootfs, setuid bits are dropped, device nodes skipped (ADR-0021). HTTPS with WebPKI roots; plain HTTP only for a registry named on the command line, and never with a credential. The credential, when GET /v1/me carried one, goes to the registry's token endpoint as HTTP Basic, or on the content when the registry challenges with Basic (ADR-0022). In a gateway-era environment the registry is the mirror on the segment, reached at layer 2 through the host table's allowance (ADR-0029); the broker refused any other registry at the claim. For a registry that is a placed audience (ADR-0043) the guest does not hold or present a credential at all: the pull goes through the claim's egress proxy and the gateway places it (rel-guest-pull-egress-proxy, rel-envoy-inject-registry); the operator-held credential of ADR-0022 stays for a deployment that accepts it and is not used in a deployment that stores no credential in a Kubernetes Secret. ADR-0063 (implemented 2026-11-22): in a gateway-era environment this connection goes away. Every pull goes through the claim's egress proxy and a gateway (rel-guest-pull-egress-proxy), the segment reach is refused with the rest of registries[], and the host table admits no registry address; the relationship then holds for a direct environment (no gateways) only.

Plain HTTP on loopback, the jail's only route out (ADR-0025): GET /<host>[:<port>]/<path> with Authorization: Bearer $MEDIATORE_TOKEN, the phantom; the proxy answers 401 for any other bearer, 403 outside the audience's rules, 404 for a host outside the claim's routes. Landlock admits this port only in the workload's process (ADR-0024) and the uid-keyed table drops packets to it from any other uid (ADR-0020).

POST /v1/token over the claim SVID, by the egress proxy since ADR-0025 (the workload before it): one audience per request, from the claim's allowlist, capped at 15 minutes, never a refresh token; fetched when a request needs it and cached until shortly before its expiry. An audience via: none is refused (403 no_credential, ADR-0025 decision 8): its route carries no credential and the proxy never asks. An audience via: secret (ADR-0032) answers the operator's credential read from a mounted Secret at the broker's start, with the header it goes in and expires_at at now plus max_ttl, so the proxy asks again through the same gate; the value is logged nowhere. Rate-limited per claim (token.rate_per_minute, 429 beyond it) ahead of any upstream call (ADR-0013). With egress gateways this connection too runs through a gateway's control relay, the claim SVID's mutual TLS end to end inside it (ADR-0027 decision 3). ADR-0070 decision 3 (implemented 2026-11-27): the broker classifies the refusals it already gives a claim identity, changing no answer byte: foreign_route (a claim on a node or gateway route), unknown_route, no_record (a claim uid with no record at all) and audience_outside_rendered (an audience in no route of the claim's rendered; a claim with nothing rendered is not judged). Each is report by default; set to trip, a claim-scoped class writes tripped (kind protocol, source peer) and releases the claim as ADR-0069 decision 9 does.

GET /v1/gateway/claims/{uid} over SPIFFE mTLS with the authorizer's SVID, spiffe://<td>/gateway/authorizer (ADR-0028 decision 4 as amended by ADR-0053 decision 3: the sandbox listener admits that identity beside node and claim identities, and no longer the listeners' spiffe://<td>/gateway). The answer is the claim's allowlist, the union of its audiences' egress sorted and deduplicated, exactly what GET /v1/me hands the guest, with the claim's deadline; since ADR-0030, when policy.egress is enforce, the union also holds the direct egress of the claim's verified, unexpired notaio bundle (found by the policy uid on the record, exact host:port entries without rules only, and since ADR-0054 only when the bundle's signed namespace is one of the sources of the record's namespace at the time of the ask; a bundle outside them is treated as missing, audience endpoints only, a placed credential refused), and in shadow, the default, only the log differs; a node, a claim, or anything under the gateway path is refused; a pending, released, expired or unknown claim is 404, which the authorizer takes as deny and drop the cache. Nothing is cached broker-side; the authorizer's bounded per-claim cache is the gateway's (crates/mediatore-gateway), asking over this route with a client built per ask from the current SVID, each ask bounded at five seconds. ADR-0070 decision 3 (implemented 2026-11-27): an ask about a uid the store holds no record of, live or ended, is classified claim_never_issued; the 404 is unchanged. The authorizer's classes are recorded only, whatever the configuration says: every gateway shares the one identity.

POST /v1/gateway/decisions over the same SPIFFE mTLS and the same authorizer SVID as the claim-egress ask (ADR-0062): the gateway's tunnel and inject decisions about claims, batched every two seconds or at 256, off the decision's path (a bounded queue, no retry), under a gateway name the gateway declares itself (attribution, not authentication: every authorizer has the one identity). The broker refuses a batch of the wrong shape whole (400 invalid_decisions), writes one info line per decision otherwise, and stores nothing. Never a path, a query, a header or a credential. ADR-0070 decision 8 (implemented 2026-11-27): the batch gains probes, at most 64, the host table's drop counts read on the gateway since its last batch (the class gateway_port or gateway_output, a count, the port, the source address for gateway_port, the local user for gateway_output), each one warn line at the broker, recorded unattributed and never ending anything. And a reported deny whose authority is in no route or destination of the claim's rendered is classified deny_outside_rendered (a claim with nothing rendered is not judged, a deny for a route rendered and since narrowed is not a class): it records only, since the claim it names is the authorizer's word, and trip on it refuses the start. At most 20 batches a second per gateway identity (429 too_many_batches beyond, nothing logged or judged) and at most 4 batches judged at once. The channel stays lossy.

The forwarder's tunnel (ADR-0028 decisions 3 and 7, a dialer inside the egress proxy by ADR-0027 decision 8): TCP to a gateway's sandbox address and data port, TLS 1.3 on the sandbox leg's configuration (X25519MLKEM768 only) presenting the claim SVID and verifying the gateway as exactly spiffe://<td>/gateway, CONNECT host:port for the upstream the request names, the upstream's own TLS inside the tunnel end to end. The list from GET /v1/me walked from a random start per connection, a connect or handshake failure or the gateway's own 5xx moving to the next (decision 7 as amended 2026-11-09), a 4xx the verdict and final (502 gateway_refused at the workload, the authorizer's code in the log; gateway_unreachable when none carried it). The lists the forwarder is given leave out the host of a gateway-placed audience (ADR-0040 decision 11): the only path to such a host is the inject listener, where the rules are enforced and the credential placed. Proven against a stand-in gateway in crates/mediatore/tests/e2e_forward.rs and against the real Envoy in kind. ADR-0063 adds the image pull: for a registry on a tunnelled route the pull listener's requests go through the same tunnel, under the claim's SVID, decided by the authorizer against the claim's allowlist like any other CONNECT.

The admitted tunnel: Envoy resolves the CONNECT authority on its own resolver and connects from the egress address to the host:port the authorizer allowed for that claim, relaying the bytes untouched (no interception, ADR-0028 decisions 5 and 9); the TLS inside is the proxy's with the downstream API. One access-log line per tunnel: the peer's SPIFFE ID, the authority, the status, the flags, bytes each way.

A pool VM's bootstrap connections, as ciphertext (ADR-0027 decisions 2 and 3, ADR-0037): the SPIRE agent's attestation and renewals to the relay's 3129, the guest's node session and the egress proxy's claim session to its 3130, and the boot-time fetch of the SPIRE bundle (curl, the endpoint's own hostname as the pin) to its 3131, and the guest's image pull (root's, the registry's own name as the pin) to its 3132 (ADR-0038); each sandbox source bounded by the host table's connection cap (decision 5). ADR-0063 removed the 3132 leg: the image pull leaves the relay for the claim's egress proxy and the gateway's data or inject port; the relay keeps the identity plane's three legs, which carry no workload byte.

The relay's fixed SPIRE upstream, by address, from the gateway's egress interface: the attestation's TLS passes through unread (ADR-0027 decision 3). The network admits the gateways' egress addresses on this port and nothing from the sandbox range.

The relay's fixed bundle upstream, by address, from the gateway's egress interface: the SPIRE servers' bundle endpoint (https_web profile), whose web PKI certificate the pool VM's fetch verifies itself against the endpoint's hostname, so the relay passes the TLS through unread and could not forge the reply (ADR-0037). The network admits the gateways' egress addresses on this port and nothing from the sandbox range.

The relay's fixed broker upstream, by address, from the gateway's egress interface: the node's and the claim's mutual TLS with the sandbox listener pass through unread (ADR-0027 decision 3); the broker verifies the peer's SVID exactly as before and sees the relay's source address.

The proxy forwards the workload's request to the downstream API over TLS 1.3 to the Mozilla roots or to the audience's own CA (audiences[].ca_file, carried on the route), at an endpoint the audience's egress list names (audiences[].egress, returned by GET /v1/me as routes; ADR-0020, ADR-0025), the phantom replaced by the audience-scoped token; the API's audit log records both the user and the broker (azp / act). HTTP/1.1, bodies streamed, one upstream connection per request.

The subject a claim is issued for; the user only ever sees their own claims. An ended claim stays on its AgentSandbox for store.retention_secs, then is swept with the audit line in the log (ADR-0034). Since ADR-0045 the user also reads, through the broker and only for their own claims, the workload output the broker stored (data-asset-workload-output), for the claim's life and its retention window after.

Seal and unseal of refresh material (ADR-0015): encrypt when a session is parked at claim creation, decrypt and encrypt again on every token issue (the refresh of ADR-0013), under a derived transit key with a context that binds the sandbox UID and, since ADR-0057, the slot (the issuer's session, or a delegation with its audience); an envelope sealed before it is bound to the bare UID and still opens. Since ADR-0052 also of a claim's stored workload output: one encrypt per ingested batch (POST /v1/me/logs) and a decrypt for each blob a read of GET /v1/claims/{name}/logs returns (at most four in flight, newest first for a tail, none for blobs behind a cursor), with the context 'mediatore-logs' plus the claim UID so a session ciphertext and an output blob never open as each other; the startup probe covers that context too. The broker logs in with its projected ServiceAccount token (audience openbao) and keeps the OpenBao token in memory until its lease ends. TLS 1.3 verified against store.sealing.transit.ca_file; a probe seal at startup fails the process on a wrong role, policy or key. With issuers[].entra.transit (ADR-0016) the broker also asks transit to sign its client assertion for Entra (PSS, SHA-256) with an RSA key that never leaves OpenBao.

A platform audience's credential (ADR-0055 decision 5, built; read and logged under shadow, served under bundles): a KV v2 read, GET /v1/<mount>/data/<path>, with the same Kubernetes-auth login as transit, configured under policy.audience_definitions.openbao. The mount, path and key come from the signed platform definition; a team audience never names an OpenBao path (notaio L023, refused again by the broker). Read every credential_refresh_secs; a failed read keeps the last good value for two periods, then none. The OpenBao policy grants read on the platform's audience paths and nothing else.
Declared registration entries are state the watcher owns and the controller manager consumes; a sweep deletes any whose claim is gone.

ADR-0031: the server's CA is an intermediate OpenBao's PKI engine signs at root/sign-intermediate every ca_ttl (24h); the server authenticates with a projected ServiceAccount token (Kubernetes auth, audience openbao) to a role whose policy allows that one path, and every signing is in OpenBao's audit log. The trust bundle the server publishes, hence the one a deployment's layer hands every member, is the PKI root: a layer stays good for the root's life, not for one ca_ttl. In the homelab collapse this is the upstream authority ADR-0005 names for the root server.

For a route with credential: gateway (ADR-0040 decision 7) the guest's egress proxy does not tunnel and never calls POST /v1/token: it checks the phantom and the rules as before, strips the phantom, and sends the request in origin form with Host: <audience host> (no port) and no credential, over the claim-SVID mutual TLS 1.3 dialler the forwarder already has, to a gateway's INJECT_PORT (carried on the route by GET /v1/me), streaming the body and returning the response unchanged, failing over to the next gateway on a connection failure only; a response carrying x-mediatore-refusal is the gateway's own refusal and becomes 502 gateway_refused (ADR-0040 decision 12). The workload and the jail are untouched; the sandbox uid's table gains gateway:INJECT_PORT for a claim with such a route and only then, and the pool VM's host table (MEDIATORE_INJECT_PORT in the guest env) admits each gateway at that port for every uid (decision 13). ADR-0043 adds one use: the guest's pull of a private image goes by the same route, as a read-only request to the registry's host (rel-guest-pull-egress-proxy).

The gateway originates TLS to the audience (ADR-0040 decision 3), only for an exact authority in the fixed INJECT_ENDPOINTS list and only after the authorizer's OK: the request leaves with the credential header the authorizer wrote. No certificate authority is minted or trusted for the workload's traffic anywhere: this is origination to a fixed list for an opt-in audience, not interception of a tunnel (ADR-0028 decision 9 stays). The gateway's routable interface must be allowed to reach the host by the datacenter's firewall (an external control).

envoy-inject's ext_authz call (ADR-0040 decisions 4 and 6): gRPC over a unix socket, inject/inject.sock (a directory of its own, setgid 2750 owned by mediatore-gateway and the group envoy-inject so the socket inherits that group, socket 0660; the authorizer's flags are --check-socket, --inject-socket and --socket-dir-mode 2750, and the two sockets never share a directory), the only channel on which the authorizer answers an inject question. The check carries what Envoy fills from the verified connection and the request (source.principal, method, host, path), never read from the client; the answer is OK with the credential header and extra headers, or the same 403 and stable code as for a tunnel, every refusal carrying x-mediatore-refusal: <code> (ADR-0040 decision 12) so the guest can tell the gateway's own refusal from the upstream's 403. The data-plane Envoy's own socket (check/check.sock, group envoy) can only get OK or 403, never a credential, so a compromised tunnel Envoy cannot obtain one even holding the gateway SVID.

POST /v1/gateway/claims/{uid}/credential over SPIFFE mTLS with the authorizer's SVID (ADR-0040 decision 2, ADR-0053 decision 3), body { audience }. Accepted only from spiffe://<td>/gateway/authorizer, runs the checks of POST /v1/token (the claim is live and names the audience, the same per-claim rate limit), requires the audience to be inject: gateway, and adds the policy admission /v1/token does not have (under policy.egress enforce the claim must name a policy whose verified bundle lists the audience, failing closed; shadow logs and allows), and calls the same per-backend code (secret, delegated opened from its sealed envelope, or sts); the answer carries the credential header and value (a Secret, never printed or logged), the non-secret extra headers and an expires_at at most 300 seconds ahead. POST /v1/token for such an audience is 403 placed_at_gateway, so the claim SVID on the pool VM cannot obtain the credential either. One log line per issue: claim UID, audience, subject, backend, expires_at, never the credential. The authorizer holds the answer in memory for at most min(60 s, expires_at minus 30 s). ADR-0070 decision 3 (implemented 2026-11-27): an ask for an audience that is not gateway-placed for that claim is classified credential_outside_inject; the refusal is unchanged and the class is recorded only.

The CLI reads and writes the saved item (--delegate <audience>=store) and asks for the secret at an echo-off terminal prompt (--delegate <audience>=prompt, terminal only, echo switched off through stty). No flag takes the secret, and no source reads a browser or another application's store (ADR-0041 decisions 4 to 6). TB-18 in the threat model.

The guest's image pull, through a second listener of the claim's own egress proxy (ADR-0043 decision 3, made the only path by ADR-0063): the guest starts the proxy (the sandbox user, the claim's SVID) before the pull, and root's puller sends every request to a loopback port of the proxy's (MEDIATORE_EGRESS_PULL_PORT, default 18129) that serves the one registry the claim's image names and nothing else (not_the_pull_host), with no credential, no challenge answered and no redirect followed by the puller. ADR-0063 decision 3: the listener serves the registry under whatever route the claim has for it, a gateway-placed route to the inject port (rel-egress-proxy-envoy-inject) or a tunnelled one through the data port (rel-egress-proxy-gateway), the proxy originating the registry's TLS inside the tunnel and checking its certificate against the route's CA. The route is a role: registry audience from the claim's namespace's signed bundles, pull-only (ADR-0063 decision 5): the workload's listener refuses it (404 pull_only), GET /v1/me leaves it out of the workload's routes and the sandbox uid's table does not list it, so the workload cannot fetch further images. The route's rules apply to each request before it is dialled. No jail rule lists the pull port (the sandbox uid's firewall set names the proxy's port and the claim's destinations; Landlock admits the proxy's port alone), and root's puller reaches it because the host table admits the loopback interface; the guest refuses a pull port that is the proxy's or a destination's. A proxy that fails to start fails the claim before any byte is pulled. The pull is bounded in the guest (ADR-0063 decision 9): a 10-second connect, a 60-second idle read (MEDIATORE_PULL_IDLE_SECS) and a whole-pull deadline (MEDIATORE_PULL_DEADLINE_SECS, default 900), each failing the claim before the jail with the host named; measured on kind, the proxy streams a 4 GiB layer in 3.4 MiB and the tunnel costs under 3% against a direct fetch.

ADR-0043 decision 2: for a registry that is a placed audience (audiences[]: via delegated, credential basic, inject gateway, the registry as the one egress entry, rules admitting only the registry API's read paths) the inject Envoy originates TLS to the registry's host and the authorizer's answer adds Authorization: Basic, the person's own user name and secret opened from the claim's sealed envelope. No registry token is created and no credential, the secret or anything derived from it, reaches the pool VM; the Bearer a registry would mint can live hours (measured: 9000 seconds), which is why the gateway places Basic itself (the operator's Artifactory accepts Basic on /v2/, measured 2026-11-15). The datacenter firewall must let the gateways reach the registry (an external control).

ADR-0045 decisions 4, 6 and 7: the sandbox API appends each accepted batch to the claim's Secret ring (LogStore::append_logs, KubeStore in crates/mediatore-claims; the memory ring under dev_mode), rolling to a new 64 KiB segment when the open one is full and deleting the oldest beyond logs.max_bytes; the user API reads it back (read_logs) for the owner; the leader's resync sweeps the segments of claims that ended logs.retention_secs ago or whose record is gone (sweep_logs), and the audit sweep of a sandbox deletes its segments with its session Secrets. At most two writes a second per printing claim (the batch limit); a write conflict between the two replicas is retried on resourceVersion.

ADR-0049, built: node attestation of a guest with no vTPM (the banlieue firecracker provider class, or a Cloud Hypervisor host that opted in to its attestation CA) by the x509pop attestor instead of the TPM one, in the pools the operator listed in watcher.x509pop_pools. The in-guest agent proves possession of the private key of a certificate its host signed for the guest's own key (EC P-256, the key never leaves the guest; obtained and renewed by mediatore node-cert over rel-node-cert-host-signer, the chain it returned presented as intermediates) and that chains to a CA in the per-host bundle; the agent ID is spiffe://<td>/spire/agent/x509pop/<issuer CN>/<subject CN>. The agent re-attests at about half its SVID lifetime and does not outlive its certificate (fail closed). Same transport as rel-spire-agent-server; keeps rel-spire-agent-server for every guest with a vTPM. Proven in kind against a real SPIRE server and agent (make kind-e2e-x509pop, 2026-11-27: refused without the host CA in the bundle and under its name on another key, then attested under the issuer-qualified ID), the leaf made with openssl there because a pod has no vsock; not yet from a guest booted on a Cloud Hypervisor or Firecracker host.

ADR-0049, built (deploy/spire-x509pop): the SPIRE server reads the per-host CA bundle, once, when it starts, as the x509pop attestor's static trust anchor; a leaf signed by a CA outside the bundle is refused, and a server-side call per guest is never made.

ADR-0049 decisions 9 to 11, built 2026-11-27 (ADR-0006 unchanged): for a machine of a pool the operator listed in watcher.x509pop_pools (<namespace>/<pool>, the machine's banlieue.io/pool label) the watcher declares the node entry (mediatore-node-<...>) as a ClusterStaticEntry whose parent is spiffe://<td>/spire/agent/x509pop/<issuer CN>/<subject CN>, selected by an explicit attestation method (tpm or x509pop), never guessed from the data present. The issuer CN is the host's CA name the administrator asserts on the Provider (spec.attestation.hostCa) and the subject CN is the machine's UID published on its status (attestationSubject), both control-plane facts available before the guest boots; both are validated against the path-segment alphabet before any request, and the host CA must be a CA with a path length of zero. The entry is named by the node key, the SHA-256 of the agent ID (decision 7). A listed machine with no subject, no Provider or no usable inline host CA gets no entry and never falls back to its EK. Same create and delete as rel-watcher-entries; the entries admission policy admits this second parent shape and cannot hold such a node entry's key to its parent, CEL having no hash (decision 11, threat model R-71). No admin SVID, no token minting.

ADR-0049 decisions 5 and 6 (amended 2026-11-24; banlieue ADR-0146), built on both sides: one request per connection on the guest's own vsock, port 1025, to the per-guest signer the host's banlieue provider runs (banlieue-attestation-ca): a PEM CSR and a half-close out; the PEM leaf followed by the host CA's chain (none for a self-signed host CA) back. The signer takes only the public key, sets the subject CN to the machine's UID, CA:FALSE, digitalSignature, a bounded validity, and rate-limits per guest. The peer is the guest by construction (the socket is that guest's alone), so no identity is exchanged on this leg. Built and tested on the host side for Cloud Hypervisor; Firecracker reuses the same contract. The guest's side checks the reply (size cap, PEM certificates only, the leaf for its own key and valid now) and was proven against the real signer on the build host (#168); not yet on a booted guest through the broker. Threat model TB-19.

ADR-0049 decision 5 (amended 2026-11-24), built (image/spire/agent-x509pop.conf, image/systemd/spire-agent-x509pop.conf): the x509pop agent reads the key and the certificate node-cert wrote (private_key_path; certificate_path, the leaf followed by the host CA's chain, with no intermediates_path, which SPIRE refuses when it holds no certificate) at start and at every re-attestation; the agent's unit requires the fetch oneshot, so it never starts without a certificate.

ADR-0063: an admitted tunnel to a role: registry audience's endpoint, the image pull of a claim whose registry is not gateway-placed. The same data plane as rel-gateway-downstream: Envoy resolves the authority, connects from the egress address to the host:port the authorizer allowed for that claim and relays the bytes untouched; the TLS inside is the egress proxy's with the registry, the certificate checked against the route's CA. One access-log line per tunnel, keyed by the claim SVID. A registry that redirects blobs to another host needs that host in the audience's endpoints, or the pull fails with the host named. The datacenter firewall must let the gateways reach the registry (an external control).

ADR-0069 decision 3: the guest draws the claim's tripwires at boot, before the jail starts, and holds them; a redraw replaces any entry that collides with a port, host, variable or file the claim really uses.

ADR-0069 decisions 6 and 7: a unix socket in /run/mediatore-guest/trap, a root-owned 0711 directory the jail cannot reach, the sandbox uid (the proxy's) admitted by its peer credential and only its first connection handed the draw. If the socket closes the proxy answers 403 trap to everything and exits, which ends the claim. The guest hands the proxy the drawn decoy routes and bait values at start, and under enforce tells it the moment it decides a trip, before the cut, after which the proxy answers 403 trap to everything; the proxy tells the guest of each trip (kind, trap, target, never the value) the moment it refuses the request.

ADR-0069 decision 2: TCP on loopback from the jail to the drawn decoy ports, and to 169.254.169.254:80 (decision 13), each of which the claim's table redirects for the sandbox uid to the guest's one trap listener on a port drawn per claim; nothing listens on a decoy port, and the listener names the decoy from the original destination. A completed handshake from the sandbox uid is a trip; another uid's new connection to a decoy port, and any uid's direct connection to the trap listener's port, is dropped by the claim's table, logged and counted, and never trips. Under the denied classes of decision 10, a connection to a loopback port that is neither the proxy nor drawn is reported where Landlock admits the port (it admits the proxy's, the drawn ones and 80 with the metadata decoy, so others fail in the syscall), and trips once its class is switched to trip.

POST /v1/me/trip over the node SVID through the control relay, as exit and report (ADR-0069 decision 8, implemented 2026-11-27): mode and up to 32 distinct events a minute, each a random id (idempotent on retry), the time, the kind (port, route, credential, denied), the trap's name, the target (a host, a port or an address; never a path, a query, a header, a body or the bait value), whether the target was drawn or the workload's, the containment time and a repeat count. The broker checks the node is the claim's, the shape and the rate; 501 under policy.traps off. Retried with capped backoff until 204, the guest waiting at most 120 s for it before its teardown. A denied event carries its class (loopback_port, private_range, unknown_host) in a field of its own and no trap. ADR-0070 decision 8: a registered node with no claim may send a report of kind segment events alone (pool_inbound with the source address, pool_output), which are recorded and end nothing; a segment event is an audit line only and is never put on a claim, a node's live claim included; a protocol event is the broker's own and is refused on this route. The OpenTelemetry part of ADR-0069 decision 11 is not built: no exporter exists (roadmap 15).

ADR-0069 decision 9: for each accepted trip event the sandbox API writes one audit line (the record of every event and host), folds it into status.tripwires on the claim's AgentSandbox by compare-and-set and re-merge on resourceVersion (a patch that names status.tripwires alone; built here, ADR-0064 not being implemented), and under enforce writes tripped on status.record by compare-and-set, then releases the claim: the entry retracted and the record revoked. Unlike POST /v1/me/exit the AgentSandbox is not deleted: the reconciler deletes the VirtualMachineClaim and marks the sandbox Failed with the Tripped condition; the retention sweep deletes the sandbox store.retention_secs after the release, and an exit for a tripped record writes and deletes nothing (one racing the trip reads the record again before its delete). The tripped claim's node may still ship its logs for 60 s after the trip. ADR-0070 decision 6 ends a claim through the same write and release for a claim-scoped protocol class set to trip.

ADR-0070 decision 4 (implemented 2026-11-27): on the gateway VM, the oneshot mediatore gateway-probes under a systemd timer reads and resets the host table's named drop counters and lists its dynamic set of probe sources over netlink (as its own user mediatore-probes, CAP_NET_ADMIN alone, no address family but netlink, no listener; one fixed setup step of the unit, making that directory, runs as root), and writes a summary, atomically, to /run/mediatore-gateway/probes. The authorizer, which holds no capability, reads the summary at its next flush, opening it without following a link or waiting on a FIFO, cannot write or remove it (it remembers the last file it read, so each is reported once), and sends its probes in the decisions batch (rel-gateway-mediatore-decisions). A missing or malformed summary is no probe and fails nothing. Both ends are roles of the one binary on the one VM, so the relationship is modelled on the gateway itself.

flows.name: Claim a sandbox and act as the user
flows.description: The happy path from login to a delegated downstream call: login, claim, bind, subject fetch, jail, token.

transitions.description: User logs in; receives a token with aud = mediatore.
POST /v1/claims; mediatore validates the token and derives the subject.
mediatore creates an AgentSandbox with spec.subject; its reconciler creates the owned VirtualMachineClaim and the store record keyed by the claim's UID (ADR-0008).
banlieue binds a Ready, already-attested pool member and mirrors its EK certificate onto the claim.
The watcher hashes the EK certificate's public key, resolves the node, and declares the claim's ClusterStaticEntry (admission policy checks the shape).
The controller manager renders the entry over the private socket and reports status.set; the watcher marks the claim live.

The in-guest agent fetches the subject, the workload, the egress endpoints and the pull credential for the image's registry, if any (ADR-0022), over its node SVID, creates the sb- user and mounts the per-claim sandbox tmpfs (ADR-0021).

The guest pulls the workload image into the tmpfs as the rootfs, manifest and layers verified against their digests and the manifest digest logged (ADR-0021); then it loads the nftables ruleset keyed by the sb- uid (ADR-0020), starts the egress proxy as that user with the claim's routes and a fresh phantom token (ADR-0025), and starts the jail in the VM's network namespace.
The workload calls http://127.0.0.1:3128/<host>/<path> with the phantom token; the proxy checks the host against the claim's routes and the method and path against the audience's rules.
The proxy presents its claim SVID over mTLS and trades it for a short-lived, audience-scoped token, kept in its memory only.
The proxy forwards the request to the downstream API with the real token in place of the phantom, on the user's behalf.

flows.name: Release and cut-off
flows.description: Any of four independent cut-offs stops the sandbox acting as the user; this is the ordered normal release.

transitions.description: DELETE /v1/claims (or the TTL fires). The record (status.record on the AgentSandbox, ADR-0034) is revoked: /v1/token refuses immediately.
The ClusterStaticEntry is deleted; the controller manager removes the server entry and the workload's SVID stops within the agent sync interval.
The VirtualMachineClaim is deleted (or its deletion observed).
banlieue destroys the member, vTPM included; the guest agent tears down the jail and user regardless.

flows.name: Node bootstrap: from EK certificate to node SVID
flows.description: How a fresh pool member gets the in-guest agent's identity without the broker ever listing agents or holding a SPIRE admin credential (ADR-0006, ADR-0007).

transitions.description: banlieue publishes the member's vTPM EK certificate on VirtualMachine.status (banlieue ADR-0045) before GuestReady.
The watcher computes sha256(DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo) of the EK, which is the tpm attestor's agent ID hash, and declares mediatore-node-<ek-hash> parented to that agent.
The controller manager renders the node entry; it waits in the server until the agent attests.
The VM's agent attests with the EK; on sync it receives the node entry and issues the node SVID to the guest role (unix:uid:0 and the path of the one mediatore binary).

mediatore guest registers the node over mTLS with that SVID; the broker checks the SVID's node key equals the one the registration's attestation gives (the EK hash, or the hash of an x509pop agent ID) and refuses a cloned node with 409.
The guest announces GuestReady on the hypervisor's channel; only now does the pool count the member (ADR-0019).

flows.name: A policy bundle, verified and compared in shadow
flows.description: How notaio's reviewed policy reaches the broker and what the broker does with it in shadow, the default: observe and report, never admit, refuse or mint differently (ADR-0026). ADR-0030 and ADR-0040 add the enforcing mode.

transitions.description: notaio compiles the SandboxPolicy, signs the bundle with its transit key and writes <policy>-bundle in the policy's namespace.
The broker's reflector sees the ConfigMap and verifies the envelope against policy.trusted_keys at the current time; a bundle that fails is logged with its reason and goes no further.

notaio's floor rule decides from the held floor (the same uid never goes down; a new uid only if issued after the held one); the store writes the next floor to its PolicyFloor resource only if the held one is still what was read, a compare-and-set on resourceVersion (ADR-0034), and a replica that lost the race reads and decides again.

Only after the write succeeds does the verified payload enter the cache; each sandbox naming the policy is reconciled, the name resolved only in the sources of the sandbox's namespace (policy.sources, ADR-0054; P011 outside them, P012 when two hold it), every gap between the broker's configuration and the bundle is logged with its code, and PolicyConformant is set True, False with the codes, or Unknown while no bundle has been read.

In shadow (policy.egress: shadow, the default) tokens are minted exactly as before: the comparison changes no admission, no claim and no mint. Under policy.egress: enforce the bundle's servable direct egress is served at the gateway (ADR-0030) and a gateway-placed audience must be one the policy admits (ADR-0040).

flows.name: A private image pulled with the person's own credential, which the VM never sees (ADR-0043)
flows.description: From the person's prompt to the first layer, for a registry that is a placed audience: the credential is sealed with OpenBao transit in the broker, placed by the gateway as Basic on each registry request, and the pool VM holds neither it nor any token derived from it.

transitions.description: The CLI asks for the user name and secret at the echo-off prompt (or reads the saved item, whose age limit is the claim's TTL) and sends them in POST /v1/claims delegations, as ADR-0041.

The broker seals the credential with the transit key derived from the claim's UID and stores only the ciphertext in the claim's Secret; the claim names an image on a registry that is a placed audience, so the claim must carry a delegation for it.
The guest starts the claim's egress proxy first, then pulls through it on the route only root can open; the requests carry no credential.
The proxy sends each request in origin form to a gateway's inject port over the claim's mutual TLS.
The inject Envoy asks the authorizer, which obtains the credential from the broker over the gateway SVID (rel-gateway-mediatore-credential) and answers with Authorization: Basic.
The inject Envoy originates TLS to the registry and streams the manifest and the layers back; the guest verifies every digest as ever (ADR-0021).
When the claim is released the broker deletes the sealed envelope's Secret; the authorizer's copy leaves memory with the claim.

flows.name: A one-shot workload's output read back by its owner (ADR-0045)
flows.description: From the opt-in on the claim to the owner reading the finished workload's output: capture and redaction in the VM, batches over the node SVID, the Secret ring at the broker, the owner's NDJSON read, the sweep.

transitions.description: mediatore sandbox create --logs: the claim carries workload.logs: true; a broker with logs.enabled false refuses it 501 before anything is created.

GET /v1/me returns the workload with logs: true; the guest spawns nsjail with piped stdout and stderr, redacts each line in the VM, writes it through to the console and queues it with a sequence number.

POST /v1/me/logs on the leading edge (at once after a quiet half second, otherwise every half second, or at 32 KiB; a line that has not ended goes as a partial record) over the node SVID through the control relay; the broker checks the node is the claim's, the opt-in, the shape, the size and the rate (two batches a second), stores the batch and wakes the claim's followers.
The batch is appended to the claim's Secret ring; a retried batch is a no-op; the oldest segment goes when the cap is reached and the dropped bytes are counted.
The workload exits under its restart policy: the guest flushes the queue (five seconds at most), then POSTs /v1/me/exit and the claim is released (ADR-0033).

mediatore sandbox logs <name>: the owner reads the stored output as NDJSON (stdout lines to stdout, stderr to stderr, a gap or a truncation one line on stderr) for the retention window after the claim ended; another subject is 403.
The leader's resync sweeps the segments logs.retention_secs after the claim ended, or at once when the record is gone; the AgentSandbox's garbage collection takes owned segments with it.

flows.name: A claim's image pulled through its own proxy and a gateway, under its namespace's policy (ADR-0063)
flows.description: The default pull in a gateway-era environment: the registry is a role: registry audience the claim's namespace was granted, the pull is decided by the authorizer like any other egress, and no path from the pool VM to a registry skips it.

transitions.description: The broker resolves the claim's audiences from its namespace's bundles and refuses the claim (400 registry_not_granted) unless a role: registry audience in that set covers the image's registry.
GET /v1/me hands the guest the registry route for the pull, apart from the workload's routes.
The guest starts the claim's egress proxy, then pulls through its pull listener; the route's rules are applied to each request.
The proxy opens a CONNECT tunnel to the registry through a gateway's data port under the claim's SVID.
The authorizer checks the registry's host:port against the claim's allowlist (broker or cache) and admits or refuses the tunnel.
Envoy connects to the registry and relays the bytes; the proxy's TLS with the registry carries the manifest and the layers, each verified against its digest by the guest (ADR-0021).

flows.name: A bait credential sent by a hijacked workload ends its sandbox (ADR-0069, accepted and implemented 2026-11-27)
flows.description: Under policy.traps enforce: the draw at boot, a request carrying bait refused on the VM before any byte of the bait leaves, containment on the VM, the report, the record and the release. A decoy port is the same from step 4 on, the guest's trap listener in place of the proxy (rel-workload-decoy-listeners). The gateway takes no part.

transitions.description: GET /v1/me answers with the claim and traps: the mode enforce and what each denied class does. No catalogue yet: the bundle's traps section waits on notaio, so the draw is made from the seeds, the generated and the derived entries.

The guest draws the claim's traps from the OS CSPRNG, redraws every collision, arms its trap listener and the sandbox uid's redirect of the decoy ports and the metadata address to it, and plants the bait in the jail's environment and the sandbox user's home. A guest that cannot arm starts no jail.
The guest hands the proxy the drawn decoy routes and bait values; the jail starts.
The hijacked workload sends a bait value in a request to one of its routes; the proxy's matcher finds it before the complete value is forwarded, resets the upstream stream and answers 403 trap.

The proxy forwards nothing more for the claim and tells the guest; the guest drops every packet of the sandbox uid in one nft transaction, kills the jail's process tree and flushes the workload output.
POST /v1/me/trip with the event, retried until the broker answers 204, for at most 120 s before the guest's teardown.
The audit line; tripped on the record by compare-and-set; the event folded into status.tripwires. No telemetry is exported: the OpenTelemetry part waits on roadmap 15's exporter.
The release: the ClusterStaticEntry is deleted and the claim SVID stops renewing.

The reconciler deletes the VirtualMachineClaim and banlieue destroys the member; the AgentSandbox is marked Failed with the Tripped condition and never claimed again; its record released, the retention sweep deletes it store.retention_secs later.

flows.name: A claim SVID used off-script at the broker ends its claim (ADR-0070, accepted and implemented 2026-11-27)
flows.description: A process outside the jail holds the claim SVID and asks the broker for what the egress proxy's code never asks. With the class set to trip in the broker's tripwires section: the classification, the refusal unchanged byte for byte, tripped on the record, the release, the VirtualMachineClaim deleted. At report, the default, the flow stops after step 2 with the audit line and the status entry. No bait, no decoy and no list to avoid: the trap is the request no honest build makes. The guest and the proxy take no part, since they may be what was bypassed.

transitions.description: Under the claim SVID, POST /v1/token names an audience that is in no route of the claim's rendered (or the claim identity calls a node or gateway route, or a path the router does not serve).

The broker answers exactly what the route answers today (unknown_audience, 403 or 404), and after the answer is built classifies the refusal: audience_outside_rendered (foreign_route, unknown_route), folded per class and peer into one audit line a minute. Never a path, a query, a header, a body or a token.
Off the response path: tripped on the record by compare-and-set (kind protocol, source peer, the class), an entry folded into status.tripwires, then the release of the claim.
The release: the ClusterStaticEntry is deleted and the claim SVID stops renewing; the broker refuses the revoked claim at once, the gateways within fresh_secs.

The reconciler deletes the VirtualMachineClaim and banlieue destroys the member; the AgentSandbox is marked Failed with the Tripped condition, reason protocol. There is no containment on the VM to wait for.
